<h2 id="meshery-adapters-for-performance-management">Meshery Adapters for Performance Management</h2>

<p><em>v0.8.0 Roadmap:</em> The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-nighthawk</code> adapter externalizes Nighthawk as a Meshery component.</p>

<p>Meshery Server allows users to generate traffic load tests using Nighthawk, fortio, and wrk2. Using the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-nighthawk</code> adapter, you can schedule, control, and execute performance tests.</p>

<p>Run the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-nighthawk</code> adapter as an externalized load generator when you:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Need a smaller sized container image for Meshery. Nighthawk binaries are dynamically linked (C++) and need other dependencies to work. This causes bloat in Meshery Server’s image, which doesn’t need them.</li>
  <li>Need <em>adaptive load control</em> of your performance tests, controlling the variability by which the system under test receives load.</li>
  <li>Need <em>distributed load testing</em> and the ability to horizontally scale Nighthawk, using Nighthawk’s execution forwarding service and results sink.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="adapter-deployment-and-registration">Adapter Deployment and Registration</h2>

<p>Like every Meshery component, Meshery Adapters use MeshKit.</p>

<h3 id="adapter-faqs">Adapter FAQs</h3>

<h4 id="is-each-meshery-adapter-made-equal">Is each Meshery adapter made equal?</h4>

<p>No, different Meshery adapters are written to expose the unique value of each cloud native infrastructure. Consequently, they are not equally capable just as each cloud native infrastructure is not equally capable as the other. Each Adapter has a set of operations which are grouped based on predefined operation types. See the <a href="/v0.8/extensibility">extensibility</a> page for more details on adapter operations.</p>

<h4 id="how-can-i-create-a-new-adapter">How can I create a new adapter?</h4>

<p>Yes, see the <a href="/v0.8/extensibility">extensibility</a> documentation for details how to create a new Meshery Adapter. See the Meshery Adapter Template repository as boilerplate for your new adapter.</p>

<h4 id="do-adapters-have-to-be-written-in-golang">Do adapters have to be written in Golang?</h4>

<p>No. Adapters must interface with Meshery Server via gRPC. Which language is used in that adapter is the prerogative of a given adapter’s maintainers.</p>

<h4 id="can-i-run-more-than-one-instance-of-the-same-meshery-adapter">Can I run more than one instance of the same Meshery adapter?</h4>

<p>Yes. The default configuration of a Meshery deployment includes one instance of each of the Meshery adapters (that have reached a stable version status). You may choose to run multiple instances of the same type of Meshery adapter; e.g. two instances of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery-istio</code> adapter. To do so, modify ~/.meshery/meshery.yaml to include multiple copies of the given adapter.</p>

<p>See the “<a href="/v0.8/installation/multiple-adapters">Multiple Adapters</a>” guide for more information.</p>

$(document).ready(function() {

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });

   <a href="/v0.8/">home</a>

</div>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > broker -->

            </li>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Broker</h1>
           <p>Broker is a custom Kubernetes controller that provides data streaming across independent components of Meshery, whether those components are running inside or outside of the Kubernetes cluster.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-log-viewer.svg"><img src="/assets/img/architecture/meshery-log-viewer.svg" alt="Meshery Log Viewer" /></a></p>

<h3 id="broker-faqs">Broker FAQs</h3>

<h4 id="how-many-brokers-can-run">How many Brokers can run?</h4>
<p>It is recommended to run one Broker instance for each Kubernetes cluster. However, the instance itself can be scaled up based on the incoming data volume in each cluster. The scaling is independent of the number of instances running.</p>

<h4 id="what-does-an-ha-configuration-look-like">What does an HA configuration look like?</h4>
<p>We leverage Kubernetes functionality for high availability. This means the Broker instance gets instantiated/restarted on its own when an issue occurs. In part, Meshery Operator is also responsible for keeping the Broker functional.</p>

<h4 id="what-stateful-characteristics-does-the-broker-have">What stateful characteristics does the Broker have?</h4>
<p>All the messages that are published to the Broker are persisted in-memory within the Broker instance until they are consumed. Persistent volume/disk space is not currently being used by the Broker.</p>

<h4 id="how-do-i-know-if-the-broker-is-working-how-do-i-troubleshoot-the-broker">How do I know if the Broker is working? How do I troubleshoot the Broker?</h4>
<p>To check if your Broker instance is running smoothly (it’s deployed as a Kubernetes StatefulSet), follow these quick checks:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Confirm that the Broker pods are running.</li>
  <li>Verify your cluster supports <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LoadBalancer</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NodePort</code> service types.</li>
  <li>Make sure the Meshery Server can reach the Broker service.</li>
</ul>

<p>Still seeing issues? The <strong><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/troubleshooting/meshery-operator-meshsync">Meshery Troubleshooting Guide</a></strong> covers common problems with the Broker, MeshSync, and Operator — and offers clear steps to resolve them.</p>
   <br/>


        </div>

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })

        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {

          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Catalog</h1>
           <p><a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a> functions much like a cloud marketplace, providing a user-friendly interface for browsing, discovering, and sharing configurations and patterns for cloud native infrastructure. With Meshery Catalog, you can easily find and deploy Kubernetes-based infrastructure and tools, making it easy to streamline your cloud native development and operations processes. A Catolog is based on the Meshery’s <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/98560345814e4be036d9f0020759faf3202ec2e4/schemas/constructs/v1alpha1/catalog_data.json">Catalog Schema</a> with defined attributes.</p>

<h2 id="a-collection-of-design-templates">A collection of design templates</h2>

<p>Meshery Catalog functions much like a cloud marketplace, providing a user-friendly interface for browsing, discovering, and sharing configurations and patterns for cloud native infrastructure. With Meshery Catalog, you can easily find and deploy Kubernetes-based infrastructure and tools, making it easy to streamline your cloud native development and operations processes.</p>

<p>It also supports a collaborative environment, where DevOps engineers can share their experiences, feedback, and best practices with others in the community. Import cloud native patterns published by others into your Meshery Server. Benefit from and build upon each pattern by incorporating your own tips and tricks, then publish and share with the community at-large. This facilitates knowledge-sharing and helps to build a strong ecosystem of cloud native infrastructure experts.</p>

<h3 id="to-publish-a-design-to-catalog-using-meshery-ui">To publish a design to catalog using Meshery UI</h3>

<ol>
  <li>In your web browser, navigate to the designs page (e.g. https://playground.meshery.io/configuration/designs).</li>
  <li>Find your design, and click Edit to update your design’s details.</li>
  <li>Verify that your design has the appropriate technologies, description, and any cavaets or other considerations of its purpose of use listed.</li>
  <li>Click “Publish to Catalog”, and your design is queued for review and approval by Workspace administrators.</li>
</ol>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/publish-to-catalog-screenshot.png" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/configuration-management/publish-to-catalog-screenshot.png" width="70%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Workflow to publish a design in catalog</figcaption>
</figure>

<h3 id="to-create-design-pattern-using-meshery-cli">To create design pattern using Meshery CLI</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Ensure that you have <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/installation/mesheryctl">Meshery CLI</a> installed on your machine and it is configured to connect to your desired Meshery instance.</li>
  <li>Open a terminal or command prompt.</li>
  <li>Use the Meshery CLI commands to interact with the catalog. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design</code></li>
  <li>Follow the prompts or instructions provided by the Meshery CLI help.
    <ul>
      <li>Apply <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/configuration-management">design file</a>:  <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design apply --file [path to design file | URL of the file]</code></li>
      <li>Delete design file:  <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design delete --file [path to design file]</code></li>
      <li>View design file:  <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design view [design name | ID]</code></li>
      <li>List all designs: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design list</code></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/mesheryctl#cloud-native-pattern-configuration-and-management">Importing</a> a design. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl design import -f [file-path] -s [manifest | compose | helm]</code></li>
  <li>Applying <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/configuration-management#wasm-filters">WASM Filter</a>. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl filter import [file | URL] --wasm-config [filepath|string]</code></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="publishing-a-design-to-meshery-catalog">Publishing a Design to Meshery Catalog</h3>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Request to Publish</strong>: The author submits a request to publish their design to the Meshery Catalog, including a description and any relevant considerations.</li>
  <li><strong>Review by Admin</strong>: The workspace owner or admin reviews the design. They have the option to approve, deny, or request changes by commenting on the design.</li>
  <li><strong>Approval Process</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li>If the admin or workspace admin <strong>approves</strong> the design, a validation is performed to ensure the design data is accurate. Once validated, the design is published to the catalog.</li>
      <li>If the admin <strong>denies</strong> the design, feedback is provided for necessary changes. After the changes are made, the design is automatically published with appropriate versioning.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Ongoing Management</strong>:
    <ul>
      <li>The author or workspace owner retains permission to edit, delete, or unpublish their designs from the catalog at any time.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Notification for Changes</strong>: If the design no longer adds value to the Meshery Catalog, a prior notification is sent to the author, and the design may be unpublished.</li>
  <li><strong>GitHub Workflow Integration</strong>: Once approved, a GitHub workflow is triggered to publish the design to the Meshery.io Catalog.</li>
</ol>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Catalog-Publishing-Workflow.svg" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Catalog-Publishing-Workflow.svg" width="70%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Approval workflow for reviewing design publishing requests in catalog</figcaption>
</figure>

<h3 id="faq">FAQ</h3>
<details>
    <summary>
<h6>Question: Why are images invisible for some designs in the Meshery Catalog?</h6>
</summary>
<p><strong>Answer:</strong> In certain instances, the images of published designs in <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a> may not be visible due to bandwidth issues. This can occur when there are network constraints affecting the retrieval of image data. However, rest assured that the design information and other relevant details are still accessible.</p>
</details>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Help with Meshery Catalog</h4>
If you have any questions or need assistance, reach out on the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">discussion forum</a>.
</div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Database</h1>
           <h2 id="what-are-the-meshery-databases">What are the Meshery Databases?</h2>

<p>Meshery Databases function as repositories for <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a>, user preferences, and system settings. Both databases are considered ephemeral and should be treated as caches. Data retention is tethered to the lifetime of the Meshery Server instance. <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Remote Providers</a> may offer long-term data persistence. Meshery’s APIs offer mechanisms for clients such as <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code></a> and Meshery UI to retrieve data.</p>

<p>See the figure below for additional details on the supported data formats and the types of data stored.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-database.webp"><img src="/assets/img/architecture/meshery-database.webp" alt="Architecture Diagram" /></a></p>

<h3 id="components">Components</h3>

<p>Meshery Database has several kinds of database implementations to support various use cases. They are listed below:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Component</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Library</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Bitcask</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">git.mills.io/prologic/bitcask</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">SQLite</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">gorm.io/gorm, gorm.io/driver/sqlite</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');

               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

          <h1>Architecture</h1>
           <h2 id="components-their-purpose-and-languages">Components, their Purpose, and Languages</h2>

<p>Meshery and its components are written using the following languages and technologies.</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Components</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Languages and Technologies</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery Server</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang, gRPC, GraphQL, <a href="https://smp-spec.io">SMP</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/database">Meshery Database</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang, SQLite</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery UI</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">ReactJS, NextJS, BillboardJS</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery Provider UI</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">ReactJS, NextJS</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang, NATS</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="#meshery-cli">Meshery CLI</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">— <a href="/v0.8/extensions">Extensions</a> —</td>
      <td style="text-align: left"> </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Golang, gRPC, <a href="https://cloudevents.io/">CloudEvents</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Meshery Remote Providers</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left"><em>any</em> - must adhere to Meshery <a href="/v0.8/extensibility">Extension Points</a></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/wasm-filters">Envoy WASM Filters</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Rust and C++</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h2 id="deployments">Deployments</h2>

<p>Meshery deploys as a set of containers. Meshery’s containers can be deployed to either Docker or Kubernetes. Meshery components connect to one another via gRPC requests. Meshery Server stores the location of the other components and connects with those components as needed. Typically, a connection from Meshery Server to Meshery Adapters is initiated from a client request (usually either <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> or Meshery UI) to gather information from the Adapter or invoke an Adapter’s operation.</p>

<h3 id="adapters">Adapters</h3>

<p>In Meshery v0.6.0, Adapters will register with Meshery Server over HTTP POST. If Meshery Server is not available, Meshery Adapters will backoff and retry to connect to Meshery Server perpetually.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-architecture.webp" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-architecture.webp" width="50%" /></a></p>

<p><em>Figure: Meshery deploys inside or outside of a Kubernetes cluster</em></p>

<h4 id="adapters-and-capabilities-registry">Adapters and Capabilities Registry</h4>

<p>Each Meshery Adapter delivers its own unique specific functionality. As such, at time of deployment, the Meshery Adapter will register its cloud native infrastructure-specific capabilities (its operations) with Meshery Server’s capability registry.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/meshery-adapter-operation-registration.svg" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/meshery-adapter-operation-registration.svg" width="50%" /></a></p>

<p><em>Figure: Meshery Adapter Operation Registration</em></p>

<h3 id="clients">Clients</h3>

<p>Meshery’s REST API may be consumed by any number of clients. Clients need to present a valid JWT token.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Meshery-client-architecture.webp" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Meshery-client-architecture.webp" width="50%" /></a></p>

<p><em>Figure: Clients use Meshery’s <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/api#rest">REST API</a>, <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/api#graphql">GraphQL API</a>, or a combination of both.</em></p>

<h3 id="providers">Providers</h3>

<p>As a point of extensibility, Meshery supports two types of <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">providers</a>: <em>Local</em> and <em>Remote</em>.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Meshery-provider-architecture.webp" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/Meshery-provider-architecture.webp" width="50%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Meshery Provider architecture</figcaption>
</figure>

<h2 id="object-model">Object Model</h2>

<p>This diagram outlines logical constructs within Meshery and their relationships.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery_extension_points.svg" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery_extension_points.svg" width="50%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Meshery Object Model</figcaption>
</figure>

<h2 id="meshery-operator-and-meshsync">Meshery Operator and MeshSync</h2>

<p>Meshery Operator is the multi-cluster Kubernetes operator that manages MeshSync and Meshery Broker.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-and-meshsync.svg" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-and-meshsync.svg" width="50%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Meshery Operator and MeshSync</figcaption>
</figure>

<p>See the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator"><strong>Operator</strong></a> section for more information on the function of an operator and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync"><strong>MeshSync</strong></a> section for more information on the function of meshsync.</p>

<h2 id="database">Database</h2>

<p>Meshery Server’s database is responsible for collecting and centralizing the state of all elements under management, including infrastructure, application, and Meshery’s own components. Meshery’s database, while persisted to file, is treated as a cache.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-database.webp" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-database.webp" width="50%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Meshery Docker Extension</figcaption>
</figure>

<p><em>See the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/database"><strong>Database</strong></a> section for more information on the function of the database.</em></p>

<h2 id="meshery-docker-extension">Meshery Docker Extension</h2>

<p>Meshery’s Docker extension provides a simple and flexible way to design and operate cloud native infrastructure on top of Kubernetes using Docker containers. The architecture of this extension is designed to be modular and extensible, with each component serving a specific purpose within the overall deployment process.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-docker-extension.svg" class="lightbox-image">
<img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-docker-extension.svg" width="50%" /></a></p>
<figure>
  <figcaption>Figure: Meshery Docker Extension</figcaption>
</figure>

<h2 id="meshery-cli">Meshery CLI</h2>

<p>The command-line interface (also known as <a href="/v0.8/guides/mesheryctl/working-with-mesheryctl">mesheryctl</a>) is used to manage Meshery. Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> to manage the lifecycle of Meshery itself and to access and invoke any of Meshery’s application and cloud native management functions.</p>

<h3 id="statefulness-in-meshery-components">Statefulness in Meshery components</h3>

<p>Some components within Meshery’s architecture are concerned with persisting data while others are only
concerned with a long-lived configuration, while others have no state at all.</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Components</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Persistence</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/guides/mesheryctl/working-with-mesheryctl">mesheryctl</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">stateless</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">command line interface that has a configuration file</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">stateless</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">interface with cloud native infrastructure on a transactional basis</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery Server</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">caches state</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">application cache is stored in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">$HOME/.meshery/</code> folder</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Meshery Providers</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">stateful</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">location of persistent user preferences, environment, tests and so on</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">stateless</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">operator of Meshery custom controllers, notably MeshSync</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: left">stateless</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Kubernetes custom controller, continuously running discovery</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h3 id="network-ports"><strong>Network Ports</strong></h3>

<p>Meshery uses the following list of network ports to interface with its various components:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Component</th>
      <th style="text-align: center">Port</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Purpose</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery Server</td>
      <td style="text-align: center">9081/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">UI, REST, and GraphQL APIs</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">Meshery Server</td>
      <td style="text-align: center">80/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">WebSocket</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">4222/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Client communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">8222/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">HTTP management port for monitoring Meshery Broker. Available as of Meshery v0.5.0</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">6222/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Routing port for Broker clustering. Unused as of Meshery v0.6.0-rc-2</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">7422/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Incoming/outgoing leaf node connections. Unused as of Meshery v0.6.0-rc-2</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">7522/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Gateway to gateway communication. Unused as of Meshery v0.6.0-rc-2</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">7777/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">used for Prometheus NATS Exporter. Unused as of Meshery v0.6.0-rc-2</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Meshery Remote Providers</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">443/tcp</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">e.g. Meshery Cloud</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/app-mesh">Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10005/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/cilium">Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10012/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/consul.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/consul-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/consul.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/consul">Meshery Adapter for Consul</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10002/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/istio.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/istio-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/istio.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/istio">Meshery Adapter for Istio</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10000/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/kuma">Meshery Adapter for Kuma</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10007/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/linkerd">Meshery Adapter for Linkerd</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">10001/gRPC</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/nginx-sm">Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh</a></td>

      <td style="text-align: left">Communication with Meshery Server</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>

<p>See the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters"><strong>Adapters</strong></a> section for more information on the function of an adapter.</p>

<h3 id="meshery-connections-and-their-actions"><strong>Meshery Connections and their Actions</strong></h3>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Connection Type</th>
      <th><strong>Connect mesheryctl</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Connect Meshery UI</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Disconnect</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Ad hoc Connectivity Test</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Ongoing Connectivity Test</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Synthetic Check</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Deploy mesheryctl</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Undeploy mesheryctl</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Deploy Meshery UI</strong></th>
      <th><strong>Undeploy Meshery UI</strong></th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Kubernetes clusters</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system start</code></td>
      <td>Upload kubeconfig</td>
      <td>Click “X” on chip</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip</td>
      <td>Yes, via MeshSync</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Grafana Servers</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>Enter IP/hostname into Meshery UI</td>
      <td>Click “X” on chip</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Prometheus Servers</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>Enter IP/hostname into Meshery UI</td>
      <td>Click “X” on chip</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip</td>
      <td>Yes, when metrics are configured in a dashboard</td>
      <td>Yes</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>No</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a></td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system check</code></td>
      <td>Server to Adapter on every UI refresh</td>
      <td>Click “X on” chip</td>
      <td>Server to Adapter every click on adapter chip in UI</td>
      <td>Server to Adapter every 10 seconds</td>
      <td>-</td>
      <td>Yes, as listed in meshconfig contexts</td>
      <td>Yes, as listed in meshconfig contexts</td>
      <td>Toggle switch needed</td>
      <td>Toggle switch needed</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a></td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system check</code></td>
      <td>Upon upload of kubeconfig</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip in UI to Server to Kubernetes to Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>-</td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system start</code></td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system stop</code></td>
      <td>Upon upload of kubeconfig &amp; Toggle of switch</td>
      <td>Toggle of switch</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a></td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system check</code></td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip in UI to Server to Kubernetes to Meshery Operator to MeshSync</td>
      <td>Managed by Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Broker</a></td>
      <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system check</code></td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>No</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip in UI to Server to Brokers exposed service port</td>
      <td>NATS Topic Subscription</td>
      <td>On click of connection chip</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
      <td>follows the lifecycle of Meshery Operator</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p><br /></p>

<p>Please also see the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q-aayRqx3QKIk2soTaTTTH-jmHcVXHwNYFsYkFawaME/edit#heading=h.ngupcd4j1pfm">Troubleshooting Toolkit</a> and the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.iot/meshery-v0-7-0-connection-states-kubnernetes-design-review/958">Meshery v0.7.0: Connection States (Kubnernetes) Design Review</a></p>
   <br/>

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {

        <div class="td-content">
           <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;">
    <div style="flex: 4;">
        <h1>MeshSync</h1>
        <p>
        MeshSync is a custom Kubernetes controller that provides tiered discovery and continual synchronization with Meshery Server as to the state of managed multi-cloud and cloud native infrastructure. It operates in one of two modes: operator or embedded. When it runs in operator mode, it is managed by the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a>.
        </p>
    </div>
</div>

<h3 id="key-features">Key Features</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Greenfield and Brownfield Support</strong>: MeshSync discovers and identifies infrastructure whether you’re starting from scratch (greenfield) with Meshery performing the initial deployment of your infrastructure or bringing in Meshery to manage your existing infrastructure (brownfield).</li>
  <li><strong>Real-time / Event-driven Status</strong>: MeshSync subscribes to updates from your platform and listens for state changes, understanding that changes to managed infrastructure may be done out of band from Meshery.</li>
  <li><strong>Scalable and Performant</strong>: Meshery’s event-driven approach ensures speed and scalability. You have control over the depth of object discovery to manage large clusters efficiently. MeshSync’s working snapshot of the state of each cluster under management is stored in the Server’s local database and continuously refreshed.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="discovery">Discovery</h2>

<p>MeshSync supports both greenfield and brownfield discovery of infrastructure. Greenfield discovery manages infrastructure created and managed entirely by Meshery, while brownfield discovery identifies separately created infrastructure.</p>

<h3 id="brownfield-discovering-existing-resources">Brownfield: Discovering existing resources</h3>

<p>The resources that are present inside the cluster are discovered efficiently with the help of pipelines. The data is constructed in a particular format specific to Meshery and published across to different parts of the architecture.</p>

<h3 id="greenfield-tracking-newly-created-resources">Greenfield: Tracking newly created resources</h3>

<p>Meshery earmarks infrastructure for which it is the original lifecycle manager. In other words, Meshery tags the resources it creates. In Kubernetes deployments, earmarking is performed using annotations, notably the key/value pair:</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">designs.meshery.io: &lt;design-id&gt;</code></p>

<p>The propagation of the labels and annotations to the native k8s resources would be the responsibility of the workload/trait implementer.
The following annotations are added to resources that are created by Meshery Server.</p>

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="na">Labels</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="pi">-</span> <span class="s">resource.pattern.meshery.io/id=&lt;uuid&gt;</span> <span class="c1"># unique identifier for the design</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="identifying-infrastructure-under-management">Identifying Infrastructure under Management</h2>

<p>Supplied by Meshery Server, MeshSync uses composite fingerprints to uniquely and positively identify managed infrastructure, capturing essential characteristics like versions and configurations.</p>

<h3 id="composite-fingerprints">Composite Fingerprints</h3>

<p>Fingerprinting, the process of positively identifying and classifying resources, is performed using a set of predefined attributes that have been designated as unique to that type of resource. For example:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Prometheus typically offers metrics on 9090/tcp, but not always.</li>
  <li>Prometheus is typically deployed from a prebuilt container offered by the open source project, but not always.</li>
</ul>

<p>See Connection State Management for additional information.</p>

<p>Fingerprinting is the act of uniquely identifying managed infrastructure, their versions and other specific characteristics.</p>

<p>As a guiding principle, each set of composite fingerprints uses the same identifiers that each element management tool uses to identify itself (e.g., istioctl version).</p>

<p>Creating a composite set of keys involves using the builder pattern. For example:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Images</li>
  <li>CRDs</li>
  <li>Deployment</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="configuration">Configuration</h2>

<h3 id="subscribing-to-eventschanges-on-every-component">Subscribing to events/changes on every component</h3>

<p>The informer in MeshSync actively listens to changes in resources and updates them in real time based on the informer configuration in the CRD.</p>

<h2 id="subscription-status-and-health">Subscription Status and Health</h2>

<h3 id="flushing-meshsync">Flushing MeshSync</h3>

<h3 id="synthetic-test-of-meshsync">Synthetic Test of MeshSync</h3>

<p><em>TODO: Include an example of how to invoke this built-in check.</em></p>

<h2 id="scalability-and-performance">Scalability and Performance</h2>

<p>One Meshery Operator and one MeshSync are deployed to each Kubernetes cluster under management.</p>

<h2 id="tiered-discovery">Tiered Discovery</h2>

<p>Kubernetes clusters may grow very large with thousands of objects on them. The process of positively identifying and classifying resources by type, aligning them with Meshery’s object model can be intense. Discovery tiers (for speed and scalability of MeshSync) successively refine the process of infrastructure identification (see <a href="#composite-fingerprints">Composite Fingerprints</a>).</p>

<p>For efficient management of large Kubernetes clusters, MeshSync uses tiered discovery. This approach progressively refines the identification of relevant infrastructure, optimizing the speed and scalability of MeshSync. You have control over the depth of object discovery, enabling you to strike the right balance between granularity and performance for efficient cluster management.</p>

<h2 id="event-driven-implementation">Event-Driven Implementation</h2>

<p>Meshery’s event-driven approach ensures high-speed operations, making it suitable for managing both small and large clusters. <a href="./broker">Meshery Broker</a> uses NATS as the messaging bus to ensure continuous communication between MeshSync and Meshery Server. In case of connectivity interruptions, MeshSync data is persisted in NATS topics.</p>

<h2 id="meshsync-deployment-mode">MeshSync deployment mode</h2>

<p>MeshSync operates in one of two modes: operator or embedded.</p>

<h2 id="operator-mode-default">Operator mode (default)</h2>

<p>When it runs in operator mode, it is managed by the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a>.</p>

<h2 id="embedded-mode">Embedded mode</h2>

<p>When it runs in embedded mode, it is integrated into the Meshery Server as a library and no additional resources are deployed to the managed cluster.</p>

<h2 id="mode-selection-and-switch">Mode selection and switch</h2>

<p>The user selects the deployment mode when creating a new Kubernetes connection (submitting a kube config). The selection is applied to all contexts from the submitted config.</p>

<p>The user can switch the deployment mode per connection on the connections list page.</p>

<p>When the deployment mode is switched from operator to embedded: the operator is undeployed from the managed cluster, and the MeshSync library routine is started inside the Meshery Server for the managed cluster.</p>

<p>When the deployment mode is switched from embedded to operator: the MeshSync library routine is stopped for the managed cluster, and the operator is deployed to the managed cluster.</p>

<h2 id="meshsync-faqs">MeshSync FAQs</h2>

<h2 id="how-to-configure-meshsyncs-resource-discovery-behavior-can-specific-uninteresting-resources-be-blacklisted">How to configure MeshSync’s resource discovery behavior: Can specific, “uninteresting” resources be blacklisted?</h2>

<p>MeshSync is managed by <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Meshery Operator</a>, which watches for changes on the meshsync CRD for changes and updates the deployed MeshSync instance accordingly. You can blacklist specific Kubernetes resources from being discovered and watched by MeshSync. In order to identify the list of one or more resources for MeshSync to ignore, update the meshsync CRD using kubectl:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Download the CRD with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl get crd meshsyncs.meshery.io -o yaml &gt; meshsync.yaml</code></li>
  <li>Open the downloaded file and edit the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">informer_config</code> field to blacklist the resource types you don’t want updates from.</li>
  <li>Apply the new definition with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubectl apply -f meshsync.yaml</code></li>
</ul>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Still seeing issues?</h4>
Check the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/troubleshooting/meshery-operator-meshsync"><strong>Meshery Troubleshooting Guide</strong></a> for help with common issues.
</div>

<h2 id="roadmap">Roadmap</h2>

<h2 id="non-kubernetes-deployments">Non-Kubernetes Deployments</h2>

<p>Even if you’re not using Kubernetes, Meshery empowers you to manage your infrastructure efficiently, providing a unified solution for different deployment environments.</p>

<h2 id="recap">Recap</h2>

<p>MeshSync maintains an up-to-date snapshot of your cluster, ensuring you always have an accurate view of your infrastructure. This snapshot is refreshed in real-time through event-based updates. Whether you’re starting fresh or adopting Meshery into existing setups, MeshSync supports both greenfield and brownfield discovery of your environment.</p>

   <br/>

$(document).ready(function() {

        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);

<h1 id="meshery-operator-">Meshery Operator <img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/B203EFA85E89491B.png" width="30" height="35" style="display:inline" /></h1>

<p>Meshery Operator is a Kubernetes Operator that deploys and manages the lifecycle of two Meshery components critical to Meshery’s operation of Kubernetes clusters. Deploy one Meshery Operator per Kubernetes cluster under management - whether Meshery Server is deployed inside or outside of the clusters under management.</p>

<h2 id="deployments">Deployments</h2>

<p>It is recommended to deploy one Meshery Operator per cluster.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-and-meshsync.svg"><img src="/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-and-meshsync.svg" alt="Meshery Operator and MeshSync" /></a></p>

<h3 id="initialization-sequence">Initialization Sequence</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-deployment-sequence.svg"><img src="/assets/img/architecture/meshery-operator-deployment-sequence.svg" alt="Meshery Operator and MeshSync" /></a></p>

<h2 id="controllers-managed-by-meshery-operator">Controllers managed by Meshery Operator</h2>

<h3 id="broker-controller">Broker Controller</h3>

<p>Meshery Broker is one of the core components of the Meshery architecture. This controller manages the lifecycle of the Broker that Meshery uses for data streaming across the cluster and the outside world.</p>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Meshery Broker</a> for more information.</p>

<h3 id="meshsync-controller">MeshSync Controller</h3>

<p>MeshSync Controller manages the lifecycle of MeshSync that is deployed for resource synchronization for the cluster.</p>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a> for more information.</p>

<h2 id="operator-faqs">Operator FAQs</h2>

<h3 id="when-is-meshery-operator-deployed-and-when-is-it-deleted">When is Meshery Operator deployed and when is it deleted?</h3>
<p>As a Kubernetes custom controller, Meshery Operator is provisioned and deprovisioned when Meshery Server is connected to or disconnected from a Kubernetes cluster. Meshery Server connections to Kubernetes clusters are controlled using Meshery Server clients: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> or Meshery UI. This behavior, described below, is consistent whether your Meshery deployment is using Docker or Kubernetes as the platform to host the Meshery deployment.</p>

<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code> initiates a connection to a Kubernetes cluster when <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system start</code> is executed and disconnects when <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl system stop</code> is executed. This behavior is consistent whether your Meshery deployment is using Docker or Kubernetes as the platform to host the Meshery deployment.</p>

<p><strong>Meshery UI</strong></p>

<p>Meshery UI offers more granular control over the deployment of Meshery Operator in that you can remove Meshery Operator from a Kubernetes cluster without disconnecting Meshery Server from the Kubernetes cluster. You can control the deployment of Meshery Operator using the on/off switch found in the Meshery Operator section of Settings.</p>

<h3 id="does-the-meshery-operator-use-an-sdk-or-framework">Does the Meshery Operator use an SDK or framework?</h3>
<p>Yes, Meshery Operator uses the Operator SDK.</p>

<h3 id="how-does-the-operator-expose-information-about-broker-endpoints">How does the Operator expose information about Broker endpoints?</h3>

<p>During the broker reconciliation step (a concept from the Operator SDK), the operator reads the deployed broker Service and populates the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">status</code> field of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">brokers/meshery-broker</code> Custom Resource (CR) with endpoint information:</p>

<p>For example, for an in-cluster Meshery deployment:</p>

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="na">status</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="na">endpoint</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="na">external</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">localhost:31670</span>
    <span class="na">internal</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">10.96.49.130:4222</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>For example, for an out-of-cluster Meshery deployment:</p>

<div class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="na">status</span><span class="pi">:</span>
  <span class="na">endpoint</span><span class="pi">:</span>
    <span class="na">external</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">1e2cd15619524f569e695f648ae7c74e-0123456789.us-south-3.elb.cloud-provider.com:4222</span>
    <span class="na">internal</span><span class="pi">:</span> <span class="s">10.96.49.130:4222</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The internal endpoint is always set to the Service’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ClusterIP</code> + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clusterPort</code>.</p>

<p>The external endpoint is selected as one of the following based on the Service configuration and network accessibility:</p>

<ul>
  <li>LoadBalancer hostname (if available and not an IP) + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clusterPort</code></li>
  <li>LoadBalancer IP (if valid and not the ClusterIP) + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clusterPort</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kubeconfig</code> host + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">nodePort</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ClusterIP</code> + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clusterPort</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">WorkerNodeIP</code> + <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">nodePort</code></li>
</ul>

<p>Refer to <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/master/utils/kubernetes/service.go">meshkit/utils/kubernetes::GetEndpoint</a> function for more precise logic.</p>

<h3 id="troubleshooting-meshery-operator-and-related-components">Troubleshooting Meshery Operator and Related Components</h3>

<p>To verify that your Meshery Operator and related components are functioning properly, perform the following checks:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Ensure the Operator pods are running.</li>
  <li>Confirm that your cluster has appropriate RBAC permissions set.</li>
  <li>Validate that Meshery Server is able to communicate with Meshery Operator.</li>
</ul>

<p>If you’re seeing issues with <strong>Meshery Operator</strong>, <strong>MeshSync</strong>, or the <strong>Broker</strong>, refer to the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/troubleshooting/meshery-operator-meshsync">Meshery Troubleshooting Guide</a>.</p>

<p>Whether you’re facing installation issues, resource syncing failures, or Broker communication problems, the guide walks you through how to identify and fix them effectively.</p>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Concepts</h1>
           <p>Concepts for understanding Meshery’s various features and components.</p>

<p><!-- CONCEPTS --></p>

<div class="section">
    <a href="/v0.8/concepts">
        <div class="btn-primary">Concepts</div>
    </a>
   <!-- <h6><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical" class="text-black section-title">Conceptual</a></h6>
     <ul>
      
    </ul> -->
    <details>
      <summary>
        <p style="display:inline">
          <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical" class="text-black">Logical</a>
        </p>
      </summary>
      <ul class="section-title">
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>
          
         -  Meshery Components identify and characterize infrastructure under management.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connections</a>
          
         -  Meshery Connections are managed and unmanaged resources that either through discovery or manual entry are managed by a state machine and used within one or more Environments.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/credentials">Credentials</a>
          
         -  Meshery uses one or more Credentials when authenticating to a managed or unmanaged Connection.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a>
          
         -  Meshery Designs are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/environments">Environments</a>
          
         -  Environments are how you organize your deployment targets (whether on-premises servers or cloud services) into resource groups.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>
          
         -  Meshery uses a set of resource models to define concrete boundaries to ensure extensible and sustainable management.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/patterns">Patterns</a>
          
         -  Meshery Patterns are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/policies">Policies</a>
          
         -  Meshery Policies enable you with a broad set of controls and governance of the behavior of systems under Meshery's management.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a>
          
         -  Meshery Registry is a database acting as the central repository for all capabilities known to Meshery. These capabilities encompass various entities, including models, components, relationships, and policies.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>
          
         -  Meshery Relationships identify and facilitate genealogy between Components.
          
          </li>
          
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/workspaces">Workspaces</a>
          
         -  Meshery Workspaces act as central collaboration point for teams.
          
          </li>
          
        
      </ul>
    </details>
    <details>
      <summary>
        <p style="display:inline">
          <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture" class="text-black section-title">Architectural</a>
        </p>
      </summary>
      <ul>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Adapters</a>
            
            - Adapters extend Meshery's management capabilities in any number of ways, including lifecycle, configuration, performance, governance, identity...
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture">Architecture</a>
            
            - overview of different individual components of Meshery architecture and how they interact as a system.
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/broker">Broker</a>
            
            - Meshery broker component facilitates data streaming between Kubernetes cluster components and the outside world.
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/catalog">Catalog</a>
            
            - Browsing and using cloud native patterns
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/database">Database</a>
            
            - Meshery offers support for internal caching with the help of file databases. This has been implemented with several libraries that supports different kinds of data formats.
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a>
            
            - MeshSync ensures Meshery Server is continuously in-sync with the state of infrastructure under management.
            
          </li>
        
        
        <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/operator">Operator</a>
            
            - Meshery Operator controls and manages the lifecycle of components deployed inside a kubernetes cluster
            
          </li>
        
        
      </ul>
    </details>
  </div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
