          <h1>Components</h1>
           <p>In Meshery, a <strong>Component</strong> is a fundamental building block used to represent and define the infrastructure under management. Each component provides granular and specific support for your infrastructure and applications. Each component represents a distinct capability or feature, like a specific service, protocol, or configuration element. Components can be semantically meaningful (orchestratable) or non-semantically meaningful (an annotation).</p>

<h2 id="components-as-building-blocks">Components as building blocks</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and their packaged Components represent a standardized and reusable collection of building blocks used to describe both the desired and actual configuration of infrastructure pre and post-deployment. Beyond this, Components are used to describe non-infrastructure concepts. For example, a component might capture a comment or a visual element that you’ve placed into a Meshery Design. To aid in distinguishing between types of Components, they are categorized into two groups: Semantic and Non-Semantic components. A component is considered semantically meaningful when it behaves as a direct representation of an aspect of your infrastructure. A component is considered non-semantically meaningful when it behaves as an annotation to aid in the comprehension of your designs.</p>

<h3 id="semantic-components">Semantic Components</h3>

<p>Semantic components represent actual infrastructure and application resources that Meshery can manage. These components map directly to real resources in your environment. For example:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Kubernetes resources like Deployments, Services, and Pods</li>
  <li>Infrastructure configurations like virtual services and gateways</li>
  <li>Cloud provider resources like load balancers and storage volumes</li>
</ul>

<p>Semantic components can be deployed, configured, and managed by Meshery’s lifecycle management capabilities. They have real operational impact when used in Designs.</p>

<h3 id="non-semantic-components">Non-Semantic Components</h3>

<p>Non-semantic components are visual and organizational elements that help document and organize your Designs but don’t represent actual infrastructure. For example:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Text boxes and comments to add documentation</li>
  <li>Shapes and containers to visually group related components</li>
  <li>Lines and arrows to show logical relationships</li>
  <li>Labels and tags for organization</li>
</ul>

<p>While non-semantic components help communicate intent and organization in your Designs, they don’t result in any actual infrastructure changes when deployed. Meshery’s lifecycle management treats them as purely visual/organizational elements.</p>

<h3 id="component-properties">Component Properties</h3>

<p>Components have several key properties that define their behavior:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Model</strong>: The model that the component belongs to, defining its capabilities</li>
  <li><strong>Kind</strong>: The specific type of resource the component represents</li>
  <li><strong>Version</strong>: The API version of the component</li>
  <li><strong>Spec</strong>: The detailed configuration for the component</li>
  <li><strong>Status</strong>: The current state of the component (for semantic components)</li>
</ul>

<p>Understanding the distinction between semantic and non-semantic components helps you effectively use them to both manage real infrastructure and document your designs clearly.</p>

<p>Once registered with Meshery Server (in the <a href="./registry">Registry</a>), components are available for inclusion in <a href="./designs">Designs</a> that you create. Components can be created and published by anyone, allowing you to share your custom extensions with the community. This fosters a collaborative ecosystem where you can leverage and contribute to the growing collection of Meshery components.</p>

<p>Components having the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kind</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">apiVersion</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">model.name</code> attributes are considered duplicates.</p>

<!-- [![Meshery Components](/assets/img/architecture/meshery-components.svg
)](/assets/img/architecture/meshery-components.svg) -->
<!-- 
 @leecalcote - This is mumbo jumbo to users and needs to be re-written.

 ## Component Status

Components have a status that is represented as a `Connection` object. Both the administrative and real-time status of a component is a normalized representation of the connection's state. The status is represented as a `Connection` object because the status of a component is a *connection* to the component. For example, the status of a Kubernetes cluster is a direct reflection of a Meshery Server's connection to the cluster.

Normalizing and extracting the status of a component as a direct property of the component and putting it into a connection allows multiple systems to share the same component with different states. For example, different Meshery Servers can access the same Kubernetes cluster, but each Meshery Server has its own connection to the cluster with its own status.

Learn more about [Connections](/concepts/logical/connections).
-->

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Connections</h1>
           <p>Meshery Connections are managed and unmanaged resources that either through discovery or manual entry are tracked by Meshery. Connections can be assigned as resources to an Environment.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Connections as resources in Environments</h4>
Meshery Environments allow you to logically group related <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connections</a> and their associated <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/credentials">Credentials</a>. Environments make it easier for you to manage, share, and work with a collection of resources as a group, instead of dealing with all your Connections and Credentials on an individual basis.
</div>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Managed vs Unmanaged Connections</h4>
Managed Connections are those that are discovered by MeshSync and are managed by Meshery. Unmanaged Connections are those that are manually added by the user and are not managed by Meshery.
</div>

<h2 id="states-and-the-lifecycle-of-connections">States and the Lifecycle of Connections</h2>

<p>Meshery tracks the status of each connection throughout the connection’s lifecycle. Meshery is intentional about the currently assigned state and which state a connection may or may not transition to and from. To better understand connection states and their meaning, let’s consider an example in which you have a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Kubernetes</code> cluster with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Prometheus</code> installed.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/lifecycle-management/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg" alt="" /></p>

<h3 id="state-discovered">State: Discovered</h3>

<p>All resources discovered by <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync’s</a> multi-tier discovery or provided as part of configuration, and if Meshery can integrate, a connection with the state <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Discovered</code> will be created. However, the connection/resources are not tested for reachability/usability; i.e., Meshery has not made an attempt to connect to or manage the connection.</p>

<p>When a connection has been discovered, it will be listed in the MeshSync browser / Connections table in Meshery UI. You can self-transition a particular connection to the <a href="#state-registered">Registered</a> / <a href="#state-ignored">Ignored</a> state.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: MeshSync discovers Prometheus components and informs Meshery Server about an available Prometheus connection, but Meshery has yet to <a href="#state-connected">connect</a> and start scraping metrics.</p>
</blockquote>

<h3 id="state-registered">State: Registered</h3>

<p>The connection in this state has been verified for use and reachability but is not yet being used. Almost all reachable connections will auto-transition to the Registered state from the <a href="#state-discovered">Discovered</a> state, and it is up to the user what to do with this connection (i.e., the user needs to administratively process the connection). It can be transitioned to <a href="#state-connected">Connected</a>, <a href="#state-maintenance">Maintenance</a>, and <a href="#state-not-found">Not Found</a>.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: A user manually selects the registered Prometheus connection and transitions it to the <a href="#state-connected">Connected</a> state (i.e., the user administratively processes the connection).</p>
</blockquote>

<h3 id="state-connected">State: Connected</h3>

<p>The connection in this state is administratively processed and is being actively managed by Meshery. Users can interface with and invoke a set of actions with the connection.<br />
From this state the transition can happen to either <a href="#state-maintenance">Maintenance</a> or <a href="#state-ignored">Ignore</a> state.<br />
Auto-transition to the <a href="#state-disconnected">Disconnected</a> state will occur if Meshery can no longer communicate with the connection, which can occur due to a connectivity issue/AuthN-AuthZ/connection being deleted outside Meshery, or any other issue.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: Meshery is communicating with Prometheus APIs to scrape metrics and present it in the UI.</p>
</blockquote>

<p><em>Certain connections can auto-transition to connected state.</em></p>

<h3 id="state-ignored">State: Ignored</h3>

<p>The connection is administratively processed to be ignored from Meshery’s view of management. Meshery will not re-discover this connection even when the current user session expires.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: Meshery Server will stop/not scrape metrics from Prometheus. However, the previous data (if connected previously) will continue to exist, and the user needs to manually delete it.</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Ignored versus Disconnected</h4>
You might intentionally choose to have Meshery ignore a given Prometheus connection, explicitly leaving in Meshery’s field of view, but identifying it as a connection not to manage. This is distinctly different than a Prometheus that Meshery was managing, but has been turned off/uninstalled and now Meshery is disconnected from the Prometheus.
</div>

<h3 id="state-maintenance">State: Maintenance</h3>

<p>The connection is administratively processed to be offline for maintenance tasks. This is different from being <a href="#state-disconnected">Disconnected</a>/<a href="#state-ignored">Ignored</a>.</p>

<h3 id="state-disconnected">State: Disconnected</h3>

<p>The connection was previously <a href="#state-discovered">discovered</a>/<a href="#state-registered">registered</a>/<a href="#state-connected">connected</a> but is not currently available. This could happen due to a connectivity issue/AuthN-AuthZ/connection being deleted outside Meshery/being administratively disconnected.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: Prometheus crashed/API token provided at time of registration is revoked.</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Disconnected vs Deleted</h4>
The connection was previously connected but is unreachable due to connectivity issue/AuthN-AuthZ/connection was **deleted outside Meshery** i.e. Connection was deleted beyond the Meshery's view of management.
</div>

<h3 id="state-deleted">State: Deleted</h3>

<p>The connection is administratively processed to be deleted and removed from Meshery’s view of management. All the available/collected data will also be deleted.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Example: Prometheus metrics will no longer be accessible to you from the Meshery UI.</p>
</blockquote>

<h3 id="state-not-found">State: Not Found</h3>

<p>User tried registering the connection <strong>manually</strong> but Meshery could not connect to it or if the connection is unavailable now. User can delete the connection or try re-registering.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Not Found vs Disconnected</h4>
You might attempt to transition to Connected state but the connection is unavailable now due to being deleted/some other reason. This is distinctly different than a cluster with Prometheuses installed for `application monitoring` which was connected previously but is now unreachable from Meshery's view of management due to change in API token/similar issue.
</div>

<p><em>Connections like <strong>Registration of Meshery Server with remote provider</strong> (and a few other connection types) can self-transition to valid states.</em></p>

<h2 id="registering-connections-with-remote-providers">Registering Connections with Remote Providers</h2>

<p>To register a connection with a remote provider, you need to follow these steps:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Obtain the necessary credentials or access tokens from the remote provider.</li>
  <li>Open the Meshery UI and navigate to the Connections page.</li>
  <li>Click on the “Add Connection” button.</li>
  <li>Fill in the required information, such as the provider type, name, and credentials.</li>
  <li>Click on the “Register” button to register the connection.</li>
</ol>

<p>Once the connection is registered, Meshery will verify its reachability and usability. If successful, the connection will transition to the “Registered” state. From there, you can choose to administratively process the connection and transition it to the “Connected” state.</p>

<p>Note that some connections, such as the registration of Meshery Server with remote providers, can self-transition to valid states.</p>

<p>For more information on the different states and the lifecycle of connections, refer to the documentation above.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery-server-registration-with-remote-providers.svg" alt="" /></p>

<p>Meshery supports different kinds of connections, and each handles transitions between their statuses differently.</p>
   <br/>


        </div>
      </main>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- meshery-custom-begin
<script>
$(document).ready(function() {
  var url = "https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=meshery/meshery";
  fetch(url, { 
      headers: {"Accept":"application/vnd.github.preview"}
  }).then(function(e) {
    return e.json()
  }).then(function(r) {
     console.log(r.items[0])
     stars = r.items[0]['stargazers_count']
     forks = r.items[0]['forks_count']
     $('#stars').text(stars + " Stars")
     $('#forks').text(forks + " Forks")
  });
});
</script>
meshery-custom-end -->

          <h1>Credentials</h1>
           <p>Meshery uses one or more Credentials when authenticating to a managed or unmanaged Connection. Credentials are based on Meshery’s <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/schemas/constructs/openapi/credentials.yml">Credential Schema</a> with defined attributes.</p>

<h2 id="understanding-credentials-in-meshery">Understanding Credentials in Meshery</h2>

<p>Credentials in Meshery provide secure authentication to your infrastructure and cloud native services. They are a foundational component that enables Meshery to establish and maintain secure connections with your resources.</p>

<h3 id="types-of-credentials">Types of Credentials</h3>

<p>Meshery supports several types of credentials:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>API Keys/Tokens</strong> - For services that use token-based authentication</li>
  <li><strong>Username/Password</strong> - Basic authentication credentials</li>
  <li><strong>Certificates</strong> - TLS/SSL certificates for secure connections</li>
  <li><strong>Cloud Provider Credentials</strong> - Authentication for various cloud platforms</li>
  <li><strong>Service Account Tokens</strong> - For Kubernetes authentication</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="managing-credentials">Managing Credentials</h3>

<p>Credentials can be:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Created and managed through the Meshery UI</li>
  <li>Imported from existing configuration</li>
  <li>Auto-discovered from your environment</li>
  <li>Associated with one or more Connections</li>
  <li>Shared across team members (with appropriate permissions)</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="credential-security">Credential Security</h3>

<p>Meshery takes several measures to protect your credentials:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Credentials are encrypted at rest</li>
  <li>Access is controlled through fine-grained permissions</li>
  <li>Credentials are never exposed in logs or API responses</li>
  <li>Support for secret management integration</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="using-credentials-with-connections">Using Credentials with Connections</h3>

<p>When setting up a new Connection in Meshery:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Select from existing credentials or create new ones</li>
  <li>Credentials are automatically validated before use</li>
  <li>Multiple credentials can be associated with a single Connection</li>
  <li>Credential status is monitored and alerts are generated if they become invalid</li>
</ol>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Designs</h1>
           <p>Like a Google Doc, Designs are your primary tool for collaborative authorship of your infrastructure and services. A Design describes all the resources and their properties that you want for a single deployment based on Meshery’s declarative syntax (see <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas">Meshery Schemas repo</a>). By default, Designs are stored in your user account, but can be manually exported, programmatically snapshotted, or automatically synchronized to any OCI-compatible registry (e.g. Docker Hub, AWS ECR, and so on), or Git-based repositories (coming in v0.8). You can share designs and collaborate in real-time on their creation. Designs can be imported, exported, versioned, forked, merged, snapshotted, published, shared, embedded, templatized, and more.</p>

<p>As the deployable unit in Meshery, a Design consists of <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a> and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>. Designs are how you can describe your desired infrastructure state.</p>

<h3 id="constraints-on-designs">Constraints on Designs</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Designs belong to only one Workspace at any given time. Designs can be transferred between Workspaces.</li>
  <li>Designs can be shared with other users or teams.</li>
  <li>The user who creates a Design is the Design <strong>Owner</strong>. The Design Owner can grant other users <em>read</em> or <em>write</em> access to the Design and can <em>delete</em> the Design.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="features-of-designs">Features of Designs</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Designs can be <strong>cloned</strong>. Cloning a Design creates a new Design that is a copy of the original Design. The new Design is owned by the user who cloned it.</li>
  <li>Designs can be <strong>merged</strong>. Merging a Design combines two Designs into a single Design. 
<!-- - Designs can be forked. Forking a Design creates a new Design that is a copy of the original Design. The new Design is owned by the user who forked it. --></li>
  <li>Designs can be exported as JSON files or OCI images.</li>
  <li><a href="https://artifacthub.io/packages/search?kind=24&amp;sort=relevance&amp;page=1">Designs can be listed in Artifact Hub</a> repos.</li>
  <li>Designs can be imported:
    <ul>
      <li>as Kubernetes Manifests, Docker Compose, Helm Charts, or Meshery Designs.</li>
      <li>from individual YAML files, remote HTTP location, local filesystem, or OCI images.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Designs can be exported or embedded.
    <ul>
      <li>Designs can be embedded in web pages either as a bundle of HTML or as a React component using the <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@meshery/meshery-design-embed">meshery-design-embed</a> NPM package.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Designs can be <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensions/-snapshot">snapshotted</a>. Snapshots are immutable. Snapshots can be compared for differences between Design versions.</li>
  <li>Designs can be published or unpublished. Published Designs are available to all users of any Meshery instance through the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/catalog">Catalog</a>. Unpublished Designs can still be available to other users if that Design is made public.</li>
  <li>Designs are versioned. Each time a Design is saved, a new version is created.
<!-- - You can revert to any previous version of a Design. --></li>
  <li>Designs can be deployed. Deploying a Design involves incorporating one or more components into your Design, configuring their relationships, and deploying them to one or more Environments. By default, any user of a Workspace can deploy a Design.</li>
  <li>Designs can be deleted.
    <ul>
      <li>Designs can be archived and restored (depending upon Remote Provider)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Designs can be compared.</li>
  <li>Designs can be validated. Validation involves checking the syntax of the Design and ensuring that all the components and patterns referenced in the Design are available.</li>
  <li>Designs can be dry-run deployed. Use dry-runs (or practice run) to ensure that your design works correctly and will not result in undesired changes.</li>
  <li>Designs can be audited. Auditing a Design involves checking the Design for security vulnerabilities, compliance with best practices, and adherence to the organization’s policies.</li>
  <li>Designs can be searched.</li>
  <li>Designs can be filtered and viewed as a live-running deployment in your Environments.</li>
  <li>Designs can be sorted by name, date created, date modified, or by the visibility level (public or private) or Catalog published status.</li>
  <li>Designs can be grouped into Workspaces and shared among teams and deployed to Environment(s).</li>
  <li>Designs can be tagged by Technology and/or by Type (e.g. Deployment, Security, Resiliency, Observability, etc.)
<!-- - While there cannot be two components with the same name within a Design, however, there can be two components with the same name in different Designs. --></li>
  <li><em>(Coming in v0.9)</em> Designs can be converted into reusable Patterns. Creating a Pattern involves replacing the values of the variables in the design with the values provided by another user. Patterns can be shared with other users or teams.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="controlling-access-to-designs">Controlling Access to Designs</h3>

<p>When creating a new design, by default its visibility level will be set to <strong>public</strong>. <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Remote Providers</a> have the option of offering additional visibility levels like <strong>private</strong> and <strong>published</strong>.</p>

<h2 id="meshery-designs-and-models-explained">Meshery Designs and Models Explained</h2>

<p>Designs are the deployable unit in Meshery. <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a> are the unit of packaging for Components. Components are described in Designs. Models are not directly deployed. Designs and their Components are.</p>

<h3 id="meshery-models">Meshery Models</h3>

<p>Meshery Models represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Think of them as blueprints or templates that define the structure, components, and configurations of your deployments. These models encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions, making them essential for consistent and scalable deployments across environments.</p>

<h3 id="meshery-designs">Meshery Designs</h3>

<p>On the other hand, Meshery Designs are the practical implementations based on Meshery Models. They represent declarations of your infrastructure deployments, customized according to specific use cases, environments, and requirements. Meshery Designs allow you to create, manage, and deploy complex architectures seamlessly, leveraging the power and flexibility of Meshery Models as their foundation.</p>

<p>Designs are the blueprints for your deployments, while Meshery Models are the internal components that provide the building blocks and knowledge to fulfill those blueprints.</p>

<h3 id="using-designs">Using Designs</h3>

<p>See the following tutorials on how to use Meshery Designs for collaboratively managing infrastructure.</p>

<details>
  <summary>

  </summary>

        </li>

        </li>
        
      
      <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/deploy-apache-cassandra-with-statefulset">Deploying Apache Cassandra with a StatefulSet in Meshery Playground</a>

        </li>

          -  In this tutorial, we will deploy guest book built with PHP and Redis in Kubernetes. We will make use of Meshery Playground in an interactive live cluster environment.
        
        </li>
        
      
      <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/embedding-meshery-design-in-wordpress">Embedding a Meshery Design in a WordPress Post</a>

      <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/exploring-kubernetes-cronjobs">Exploring Kubernetes CronJobs</a>

Leveraging Meshery Playground, an interactive live cluster environment, we'll perform hands-on labs to understand the practical aspects of working with ConfigMaps and Secrets in Kubernetes.
        
        </li>
        
      
      <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/tutorials/kubernetes-deployments">Exploring Kubernetes Deployments with Meshery</a>
        
          -  Explore a Kubernetes Deployment using Meshery Playground, an interactive live environment, through a series of hands-on exercises.

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Environments</h1>
           <p>Meshery Environments allow you to logically group related <a href="#connections">Connections</a> and their associated <a href="#credentials">Credentials</a>. Environments make it easier for you to manage, share, and work with a collection of resources as a group, instead of dealing with all your Connections and Credentials on an individual basis.</p>

<h3 id="assigning-resources-to-an-environment">Assigning Resources to an Environment</h3>

<p>Assign any number of Connections to an environment whether that Connection is managed or unmanaged (see <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/meshsync">MeshSync</a> to learn more about managed and unmanaged Connections). In turn, assign any number of Environments to one or more <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/workspaces">Workspaces</a>. Connections (and any associated Credentials) that are assigned to an Environment become immediately available for use in any associated Workspace.</p>

<h3 id="sharing-resources-between-environments">Sharing Resources between Environments</h3>

<p>Environments can share resources. For example, you might create an environment named “production” and assign three connections: a GitHub connection, a Kubernetes connection, and a Prometheus connection. Subsequently, you can also define an environment named “dev/test” and assign three connections: a different Kubernetes connection, a different Prometheus connection, <em>and</em> the same GitHub connection that is also assigned to the “production” environment.</p>

<h3 id="deleting-an-environment">Deleting an Environment</h3>

<p>Deleting an environment does not delete any resources (e.g. connections) currently contained within the environment. Resources that belong to other environments will continue to belong to those other environments. Learn more about the behavior of the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">connection lifecycle</a>.</p>

<h2 id="key-features">Key Features</h2>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Logical Grouping</strong>: Environments allow you to logically group related connections and their associated credentials. This makes it easier to manage, share, and work with a subset of resources instead of dealing with all your connections individually.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Resource Sharing</strong>: Environments can be seamlessly assigned to <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/workspaces">Workspaces</a>, another essential concept in Meshery. When you assign an Environment to a Workspace, you enable resource sharing among team members. This collaborative approach simplifies the sharing of connections and resources, making it easier to work together in cloud-native environments.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="connections-and-credentials-as-resources">Connections and Credentials as Resources</h2>

<h3 id="connections-">Connections <a id="connections"></a></h3>

<p>Connections are an integral part of Environment. These are cloud-native resources that can be both managed and unmanaged, and they’re registered by the Meshery Server. Examples of connections include Kubernetes clusters, Prometheus instances, Jaeger tracers, and Nginx web servers.</p>

<p>See “<a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connections</a>” section for more information.</p>

<h3 id="credentials-">Credentials <a id="credentials"></a></h3>

<p>Credentials in an Environment are the keys to securely authenticate and access managed connections. For example, valid Prometheus secrets or Kubernetes API tokens are essential credentials for securely interacting with these managed resources.</p>

<p>See “<a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/credentials">Credentials</a>” section for more information.</p>

<h2 id="environment-lifecycle">Environment Lifecycle</h2>

<p>Environments in Meshery follow a defined lifecycle that helps maintain organization and control over your cloud-native resources:</p>

<h3 id="creating-environments">Creating Environments</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Create environments through Meshery UI or via <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl</code></li>
  <li>Give your environment a meaningful name and description</li>
  <li>Optionally add tags for better organization</li>
  <li>Start assigning connections and credentials</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="managing-environments">Managing Environments</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Add or remove connections and credentials as needed</li>
  <li>Monitor the health and status of resources within the environment</li>
  <li>Configure environment-specific settings and policies</li>
  <li>Share environments by assigning them to workspaces</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="environment-states">Environment States</h3>

<p>Environments can exist in different states:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Active</strong>: Environment is created and ready for use</li>
  <li><strong>Empty</strong>: Environment exists but has no connections assigned</li>
  <li><strong>Archived</strong>: Environment is preserved but not actively used</li>
  <li><strong>Deleted</strong>: Environment is removed but contained resources persist</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="best-practices">Best Practices</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Use clear naming conventions for environments (e.g., “prod”, “staging”, “dev”)</li>
  <li>Document the purpose and contents of each environment</li>
  <li>Regularly review and clean up unused environments</li>
  <li>Implement consistent tagging across environments</li>
  <li>Maintain separation between production and non-production environments</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="environment-security">Environment Security</h2>

<p>Meshery implements several security measures for environments:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Access control through workspace permissions</li>
  <li>Credential encryption for sensitive data</li>
  <li>Audit logging of environment changes</li>
  <li>Resource isolation between environments</li>
</ul>

<p>By following these lifecycle and security practices, you can maintain well-organized and secure environments for your cloud-native infrastructure.</p>

<h2 id="summary">Summary</h2>

<p>Environments represent a collection of resources in the form of Connections - both managed and unmanaged. Environment resources are comprised of Connections (and implicitly any Credentials used by those assigned Connections). Create and use environments to organize your connections and credentials into groups, and then make these resources available to you and your teams by assigning environments to <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/workspaces">Workspaces</a>.</p>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Logical</h1>
           <p>As an extensible platform, Meshery empowers you with a wide range of logical constructs that provide support for the majority of the systems in the cloud and cloud native ecosystems. Meshery abstracts away the system-specific requirements and helps you focus on getting things done.</p>

<h2 id="logical-concepts">Logical Concepts</h2>

<ul>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>
      
        -  Meshery Components identify and characterize infrastructure under management.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connections</a>
      
        -  Meshery Connections are managed and unmanaged resources that either through discovery or manual entry are managed by a state machine and used within one or more Environments.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/credentials">Credentials</a>
      
        -  Meshery uses one or more Credentials when authenticating to a managed or unmanaged Connection.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a>
      
        -  Meshery Designs are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/environments">Environments</a>
      
        -  Environments are how you organize your deployment targets (whether on-premises servers or cloud services) into resource groups.
      
      </li>

   
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>
      
        -  Meshery uses a set of resource models to define concrete boundaries to ensure extensible and sustainable management.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/patterns">Patterns</a>
      
        -  Meshery Patterns are descriptive, declarative characterizations of how your Kubernetes infrastructure should be configured.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/policies">Policies</a>
      
        -  Meshery Policies enable you with a broad set of controls and governance of the behavior of systems under Meshery's management.
      
      </li>

   
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a>
      
        -  Meshery Registry is a database acting as the central repository for all capabilities known to Meshery. These capabilities encompass various entities, including models, components, relationships, and policies.
      
      </li>
      
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>
      
        -  Meshery Relationships identify and facilitate genealogy between Components.
      
      </li>
      
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/workspaces">Workspaces</a>
      
        -  Meshery Workspaces act as central collaboration point for teams.
      
      </li>
      
    
</ul>

<p>The logical concepts included in Meshery establish a set of foundational constructs. Each logical construct is:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Versioned (see <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas">Schemas</a>)</li>
  <li>Extensible (see <a href="/v0.8/extensibility">Extension Points</a>)</li>
  <li>Composable (see <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/patterns">Patterns</a>)</li>
  <li>Portable (see Export/Import of <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a> and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>)</li>
  <li>Interoperable (see <a href="/v0.8/installation/compatibility-matrix">Compatibility Matrix</a>)</li>
  <li>Configurable (see <a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management">Lifecycle Management</a>)</li>
  <li>Documented (<em>you are here</em>)</li>
  <li>Testable</li>
  <li>Maintainable</li>
  <li>Secure (v0.9.0)</li>
  <li>Observable (v0.1.0)</li>
</ol>

<p>Every construct is represented in each of the following forms:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Schema</strong> (static) - The skeletal structure representing a logical view of the size, shape, and characteristics of a construct.
    <ul>
      <li><em>Example: Component schema found in github.com/meshery/schemas</em></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Definition</strong> (static) - An implementation of the Schema containing specific configuration for the construct at hand.
    <ul>
      <li><em>Example: Component definition generically describing a Kubernetes Pod</em></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Declaration</strong> (static) - A defined construct; a specific instance of the Definition.
    <ul>
      <li><em>Example: Component configuration of an NGINX container as a Kubernetes Pod</em></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Instance</strong> (dynamic) - A realized construct (deployed/discovered); an instantiation of the Declaration.
    <ul>
      <li><em>Example: NGINX-as234z2 pod running in cluster</em></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Models</h1>
           <p>Models are units of packaging for definitions of Meshery’s logical object representations. Each model is versioned and encompasses a collection of components, relationships, policies, connections, and credentials. Meshery’s internal object model provides a consistent and extensible way of capturing and characterizing the resources (applications, services, and infrastructure) under Meshery’s management. Each model is versioned and bundles definitions of any number of components, relationships, policies, connections and credentials. Additionally, models can be exported as OCI-compatible images, defining the managed infrastructure, their interrelationships, and specific management details.</p>

<h2 id="key-aspects-of-meshery-models">Key aspects of Meshery Models</h2>

<p>Models serve as the foundational packaging units for Meshery’s logical object representations. Each model is versioned and encompasses a collection of components, relationships, policies, connections, and credentials. Designed for consistency and extensibility, Meshery’s internal object model effectively captures and characterizes the resources—such as applications, services, and infrastructure—under its management. Additionally, models can be exported as OCI-compatible images, defining the managed infrastructure, their interrelationships, and specific management details.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Logical Representation:</strong> Models offer a logical representation of entities under Meshery’s management, abstracting away system-specific details.</li>
  <li><strong>Packaging:</strong> Model packages can be imported and exported as OCI-compatible images, ensuring portability and encapsulation of intellectual property.</li>
  <li><strong>Components:</strong> Components within a Model represent the capabilities of the underlying platform and are used by operators to build applications.</li>
  <li><strong>Relationships:</strong> Relationships define interactions and dependencies between components within a model.</li>
  <li><strong>Policies:</strong> Policies govern the behavior and constraints of components and relationships, ensuring adherence to desired operational practices.</li>
  <li><strong>Extensibility:</strong> Models are highly extensible, allowing you to define custom components, relationships, and policies.</li>
</ul>

<div class="alert alert-light">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Creating your own models</h4>
If you would like to create your own, augment existing models, or contribute new models, please refer to the <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing/contributing-models">Contributing to Models</a> guide.
</div>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing/contributing-models">Contributing to Models</a>.</p>

<p>As a cloud native manager that provides a comprehensive set of tools for managing multi-cloud and cloud native applications and infrastructure, Meshery needs object models that can granularly characterize a wide range of systems under management from simple applications to complex microservices architectures and their infrastructure. This document describes the Meshery Model and its constituent set of entities used to represent and manage cloud and cloud native systems.</p>

<p>Using Meshery Models, users can define and manage cloud-native systems, including applications, services, and infrastructure. Models provide a way to represent the desired state of the system, and they can be used to deploy, monitor, and manage cloud-native applications. Models are designed to be extensible, allowing users to define new constructs as needed. They are also machine-readable, allowing them to be used by automation tools.</p>

<h3 id="model-portability-and-your-intellectual-property">Model Portability and Your Intellectual Property</h3>

<p>Each model (package) can be imported and exported from Meshery Server as OCI-compatible images. This makes models portable, abstracts their complexity, and encapsulates intellectual property that you might have created while designing your own models. Model packages are versioned and bundle any number of components, relationships, policies, connections, and credentials.</p>

<p>Models are stored in Meshery’s <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">registry</a> where they can be:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Discovered and reused by teams</li>
  <li>Versioned and tagged</li>
  <li>Shared publicly or kept private</li>
  <li>Extended and customized</li>
</ul>

<p>The registry provides a central location for managing and distributing your infrastructure models.</p>

<p>Every entity type is implemented by a <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">registrant</a>. Without registrants and models, Meshery can’t manage any kind of infrastructure.</p>

<p>Most registrants configure a specific infrastructure platform (either cloud or self-hosted). Registrants vary in their capabilities. Capabilities come in the form of components, some of which represent infrastructure to be managed, and others of which represent additional functionality to augment Meshery’s behavior and deepen its feature set. Some registrants offer infrastructure-specific orchestration. For example, the Meshery Adapter for Istio offers integration with each of Istio’s addons. Other registrants offer specific services. For example, the Meshery Adapter for Nighthawk offers load generation and service performance characterization.</p>

<h2 id="design-principles">Design Principles</h2>

<p>Meshery Models adhere to several design principles, including establishing a set of constructs, clearly defining construct boundaries, allowing construct extension, reusing existing models, being user-centric, and simplifying complex networking and distributed systems. Meshery Models are designed to meet the following goals:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Comprehensive:</strong> The model should be able to represent a wide range of cloud and cloud native resources.</li>
  <li><strong>Extensible:</strong> The model should be extensible, allowing new constructs to be added as needed.</li>
  <li><strong>User-centric:</strong> The model should be easy for users to understand and use.</li>
  <li><strong>Machine-readable:</strong> The model should be machine-readable, allowing it to be used by automation tools.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="models-as-the-unit-of-packaging">Models as the Unit of Packaging</h2>

<p>Each model package can be imported and exported from the system as OCI-compatible images, making them portable (a design goal), abstracting their complexity, and encapsulating potential intellectual property that users might have invested into their models. Model packages are versioned and bundle any number of components, relationships, policies, connections and credentials. For example:</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Model Packaging</h4>
Model constructs can be packaged and exported as OCI-compatible images. This makes them portable and allows them to be shared between different environments.
</div>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/concepts/meshery-models.png" alt="Meshery Models" />
<em>Figure: Model Construct Classification</em></p>

<h2 id="key-aspects-and-characteristics">Key aspects and characteristics</h2>

<p>You might not fully comprehend the Meshery Models figure above. The following analogy offers an alternative viewpoint from which to comprehend the Capabilities Registry (where Models are imported and their capabilities registered for use).</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/concepts/meshery-models-analogy.svg" alt="Meshery Models Analogy" />
<em>Figure: Registrar’s Office and Meshery Models Analogy</em></p>

<h3 id="models">Models</h3>

<p>Models introduce various core constructs that form the foundation of the model. Some of the core constructs mentioned in the document include Components, Designs, Policies, and Relationships. Models having the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">name</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">version</code> attributes are considered duplicates.</p>

<h3 id="component">Component</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Component</a> represent entities in the Meshery ecosystem, exposing capabilities of the underlying platform. They can be registered, created, and used by users and operators. Components have definitions, instances, and associated metadata. Components having the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kind</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">apiVersion</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">model.name</code> attributes are considered duplicates.</p>

<h3 id="policy">Policy</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/policies">Policies</a> includes constructs for managing metrics, defining actions, and specifying color properties of components or designs. These constructs help in monitoring, controlling, and visualizing different aspects of the Meshery ecosystem.</p>

<h3 id="relationships">Relationships</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a> define the nature of interaction between interconnected components in a Model. They represent various types of connections and dependencies between components, such as hierarchical, network, or default relationships. Relationships have selectors, metadata, and optional parameters.</p>

<h4 id="evaluation-of-relationships">Evaluation of Relationships</h4>

<p>Meshery provides a relationship evaluation algorithm to ensure desired behavior enforcement. <a href="policies">Policies</a> can be applied to components and relationships, defining rules and actions based on predefined conditions.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Model Schema</h4>
Model constructs are defined using a schema language called Cue. Cue is a powerful and expressive language that is well-suited for defining cloud-native constructs.
</div>

<h3 id="designs">Designs</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a> are deployable units in Meshery that describe the desired infrastructure. They consist of components and patterns, allowing users to define and configure the behavior of their cloud-native applications. A design is a collection of components and patterns that represent a desired state of infrastructure. Designs are used to deploy and manage cloud-native systems.</p>

<h3 id="patterns">Patterns</h3>

<p><a href="patterns">Patterns</a> are reusable configurations that can be applied to components or designs. They define best practices for configuring and operating cloud-native application functionality. Patterns can be applied to components or designs, and they are read-only.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Metadata</h4>
Metadata provide additional details about a component in Meshery. They offer specific functionality or characteristics associated with a component, enhancing its capabilities. Metadata can be attached to components to customize their behavior.
</div>

<h2 id="versioning">Versioning</h2>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/concepts/logical/versioning-meshery-entities.svg" alt="Versioning Models" /></p>

<h2 id="summary">Summary</h2>

<p>A Model serves as a unit of packaging for Meshery’s logical object representation. Models encompass a structured framework that defines the components, relationships, policies, and other elements that constitute a system or application under Meshery’s management. Models offer a way to encapsulate the complexities of diverse systems and provide a standardized representation for management and interaction.</p>

<p>Models are a powerful way to define, package and share your infrastructure configurations in Meshery. They provide a consistent, portable format for managing cloud native systems while enabling reuse and collaboration across teams.</p>

<p>By using models, you can:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Define infrastructure in a standardized way</li>
  <li>Package related resources together</li>
  <li>Share and reuse configurations</li>
  <li>Track changes through versioning</li>
  <li>Extend and customize for your needs</li>
</ul>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Patterns</h1>
           <p>A Pattern is a templated design. Patterns promote reuse. Patterns are higher-level abstractions of designs, in which a complex design is represented as a single component, promoting consistent infrastructure management practices as it hides the complexity of its underlying design. Patterns enable you to establish best practices and propagate the use of these practices in a simple, consumable single component. Once created, a pattern becomes available for use alongside other components.</p>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Future Feature</h4>
Patterns are a roadmap item, planned for v0.9.0.
</div>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Policies</h1>
           <p>Policies offer an evaluation algorithm to ensure desired behavior enforcement. Policies can be applied to components and relationships, defining rules and actions based on predefined conditions.</p>

<h2 id="policy-evaluation">Policy Evaluation</h2>

<p>Relationships are a powerful way to design your infrastructure, and each of them is backed by one or more policies. Policies evaluate designs for potential relationships and then decide whether to create/delete/update the relationships.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/concepts/meshery-models-policy-evaluation.svg"><img src="/assets/img/concepts/meshery-models-policy-evaluation.svg" alt="Meshery Models Policy Evaluation" /></a></p>

<p>Meshery Server has a built-in policy engine, based on Open Policy Agent (OPA). Currently, Meshery Server is the only place where the policy evals occur. Policy evaluation is invoked each time a design is updated, and each time a design is imported. By default, policies evaluate for all registered relationships.</p>

<p>In any given Meshery deployment, you can reference and search the full set of registered policies (in Meshery’s internal registry) using either of Meshery’s client interfaces.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Viewing All Registered Relationships</h4>
<p>You can view all registered relationships using either Meshery UI or Meshery CLI.</p><dl><dt>Using Meshery UI...</dt><dd>Navigate to <i>Settings</i>, then to <i>Registry</i></dd>.<dt>Using Meshery CLI...</dt><dd><code>mesheryctl policy list</code></dd></dl>
</div>

<!-- There are different points in time in which policy evaluations are invoked

1. Each time the design is updated.
2. A Design/HelmChart/K8s Manifest/Docker Compose app is imported/uploaded.
3. Ad-hoc invocation from the Actions Center (coming soon). 
-->

<h3 id="how-are-conflicts-resolved">How are conflicts resolved?</h3>

<p>In the event of a conflict or tie, Meshery relies on Open Policy Agent’s <a href="https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/faq/">reconciliation behavior</a> for conflict resolution.</p>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Conflict Resolution</h4>
It may happen that certain eval decisions contain results such that two different components create a conflicting relationship with same component. While this is semantically correct, the visual representation of the relationship in such cases may be undesirable, and you may see relationships and components being redrawn depending upon how the client / Meshery UI visualizes the relationships.
</div>

<p>For an in-depth review, watch this meeting recording.</p>

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/XrLpBVsm6nk?si=j-igwtd_gQ0N61vV&amp;start=453" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Future Feature</h4>
Policy evaluation in WASM runtime is on roadmap for Meshery v0.8.3.
</div>

   <br/>
