<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];

              $(this).addClass('selected');

              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }

        <div class="td-content">
           <h1 id="meshery-registry-a-central-hub-for-capabilities">Meshery Registry: A Central Hub for Capabilities</h1>

<p>The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently <a href="#interacting-with-the-meshery-registry">access and manage registry data</a> through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).</p>

<p>As the central repository for all capabilities known to Meshery, the registry contains various entities.</p>

<details>
  <summary>Contents of the Registry</summary>
  <br /><br />
  <a href="../models">Models</a>: Blueprints defining configurations for interacting with cloud native infrastructure. They consist of operations, components, relationships, and policies.
  <ul>
    <li><a href="../components">Components</a>: Reusable building blocks for depicting capabilities defined within models.</li>
    <li><a href="../relationships">Relationships</a>: Define the nature of connections between components within a model, describing how they interact and depend on each other.</li>
    <li><a href="../logical/policies">Policies</a>: Enforce specific rules and governance for system behavior under Meshery's management.</li>
    <li><a href="../connections">Connections</a>: Managed and unmanaged resources that Meshery can interact with.</li>
    <li><a href="../credentials">Credentials</a>: Optionally, included secrets associated with connections contained in a model.</li>
  </ul>
  <br />
</details>

<h2 id="key-concepts-and-terminology">Key Concepts and Terminology</h2>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Registry</strong>: a component within Meshery that contains a database of known capabilities.</li>
  <li><strong>Registrar</strong>: The internal Meshery Server process responsible for managing and maintaining the registry.</li>
  <li><strong>Registrant</strong> (Entity Source): The source of an entity (e.g., model file, Kubernetes cluster).</li>
  <li><strong>Entity</strong> (Registree): An individual capability stored in the registry (e.g., model, component).</li>
  <li><strong>Registrant</strong> <em>(Host)</em>: A Meshery Connection responsible for sourcing and registering entities. A registrant can perform registration for their own entities, or a registrant can act as a proxy on behalf of a third-party entity source.</li>
  <li><strong>Entity</strong> <em>(registree)</em> - an entry in the Meshery Registry; e.g. a model, component, relationship, or policy. Sometimes referred to as a capability.
<!-- - **Entity Source**: an entity’s original location from which it was sourced; e.g. (source_uri is used as the flag by Meshery Server to assess whether additional support). The Entity Source should have all the information that Meshery needs to generate the components.   --></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="models-in-the-registry">Models in the Registry</h2>

<p>You will find two types of models in the registry: Static and Dynamic.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Static Models:</strong> Pre-defined models included with each Meshery release. See the full list of static models.</li>
  <li><strong>Dynamic Models:</strong> Generated at run-time by connecting Meshery to supported platforms like Kubernetes clusters or cloud providers.</li>
</ul>

<p>Each Meshery release comes with a built-in set of models automatically registered at Meshery Server boot-time. These built-in models offer a core set of entities for Meshery’s supported <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/integrations">integrations</a>. Once Meshery Server is running, and as it connects to and discovers your infrastructure, <em>dynamic models</em> are automatically generated. A given Meshery release may not include all possible models found in your environment, so Meshery automatically generates <em>and registers</em> new models and components based on the specific infrastructure Meshery is connected to. Dynamic models often lack additional metadata, such as descriptions, tags, and relationships, which are typically included in static models.</p>

<h2 id="interacting-with-the-meshery-registry">Interacting with the Meshery Registry</h2>

<p>Use either Meshery UI or CLI to interact with the Registry. Meshery UI offers a user-friendly visual interface for browsing, searching, and managing registry entries. You can easily explore available models, components, and relationships, gaining insights into their properties and connections. Meshery CLI offers commands so that you can register, list, retrieve, update, and delete models, components, and relationships directly from the command line.</p>

<h3 id="model-generation">Model Generation</h3>

<p>The process of generating a Model (and its entities) is a multi-step process and does not require use of Meshery Server. The process begins with the sourcing of the model information from an authoritative source: a Registrant. Registrants are responsible for providing all the necessary information to Meshery to generate the model.</p>

<h4 id="using-meshery-cli-to-generate-models">Using Meshery CLI to Generate Models</h4>

<p>Meshery CLI supports the generation of models from a Google Spreadsheet. The Google Spreadsheet should contain a list of model names and source locations from any supported Registrant (e.g. GitHub, Artifact Hub) repositories. The source locations can be a URL to a folder containing Kubernetes CRDs, or to a Helm Chart tar.gz, or an individual Kubernetes Manifest with custom resource definition.</p>

<p>See <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry/generate"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl registry generate</code></a> for more information.</p>

<h3 id="model-registration">Model Registration</h3>

<p>Once registered in the Meshery Registry, Models and their entities are available for use within that specific Meshery Server.</p>

<p>Meshery <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Adapters</a> are one example of a Registrant. Registrants are responsible for the registration of entities in the Meshery Registry. Adapters are responsible for the sourcing and registration of entities and the packaging of these entities into one or more models.</p>

<h4 id="using-meshery-cli-to-register-a-model">Using Meshery CLI to Register a Model</h4>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>mesheryctl model import <span class="nt">-f</span> &lt;path-to-model&gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="using-meshery-ui-to-register-a-model">Using Meshery UI to Register a Model</h4>

<p>Visit the Settings –&gt; Registry page and click the “Import” button to import a model.</p>

<h3 id="ignoring-an-entity">Ignoring an Entity</h3>

<p>You have control over whether a registered entity (model and all that the model contains) this can be an individual or team-level preference. Use the “Ignore” action to designate whether a given model is allowed to be used within a given Meshery Server deployment. Models that are ignored remain in the Meshery Registry but are not available for use within a given Meshery Server deployment.</p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Relationships</h1>
           <p>Meshery Relationships characterize how <a href="./components">components</a> are connected and interact with each other. Relationships are defined within <a href="./models">models</a> to aid in structuring the interrelationships between one or more components in a <a href="./designs">design</a> to further aid in comprehending the overall structure and dependencies within managed systems.</p>

<p>Meshery recognizes that relationships exist in various forms and that the existence of a relationship might be interdependent upon the existence (or absence) of another relationship. To support this complexity, Meshery relationships are highly expressive, characterizing the nature of interaction of interconnected components no matter their genealogy.</p>

<p><strong>Benefits of Using Meshery Relationships</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Improved Visibility:</strong> Relationships provide a clear visual representation of the connections between components, making it easier to understand the system’s architecture.</li>
  <li><strong>Enhanced Design:</strong> Relationships help you make informed decisions about component selection and placement, leading to better design choices.</li>
  <li><strong>Automated Configuration:</strong> Relationship-driven actions can automate the configuration of components, reducing manual effort and potential errors.</li>
  <li><strong>Increased Flexibility:</strong> The use of selectors, actions, and operators provides flexibility in defining and managing relationships.</li>
</ul>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Contributor Guide to Meshery Relationships</h4>
If you want to create a new relationship definition or modify existing relationship definitions, see the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-relationships">Contributing to Meshery Relationships</a> guide.
</div>

<h2 id="types-of-relationships">Types of Relationships</h2>

<p>Meshery supports different types of relationships to cater to various use cases:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Hierarchical Relationships:</strong> These represent parent-child relationships between components, where one component is a dependency of another. Parent-child relationships show clear lineage, similar to a family tree (child, parent, grandparent, etc.).</li>
  <li><strong>Sibling Relationships:</strong> These represent relationships between components that are not directly dependent on each other but may still interact or influence each other’s behavior; they describe components that share a common origin but operate independently (siblings, cousins, etc.).</li>
  <li><strong>Edge Relationships:</strong> These represent relationships that are visually depicted as edges connecting components in MeshMap. Edge relationships are used to define how components interact with each other, such as network connections, bindings, or permissions. They are also used to identify interdependencies between components.</li>
  <li><strong>TagSets Relationships:</strong> These represent relationships between components with the same label or annotation key/value pairs. Labels and Annotations are two different types of tags. Labels are often used to identify components and are visible on the design canvas. Annotations are often used to provide additional information about components.</li>
</ul>

<p>Relationships are categorized into different kinds, types, and subtypes, so that they can be expressive of the specific manner in which one or more components relate to one another. Each type of relationship can be interpreted by Meshery UI (or other <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/extensions">extensions</a>) and mapped to a specific visual paradigm for the given kind relationship. Let’s look at some examples of these visual paradigms; let’s explore examples of ways in which relationships are represented in Meshery.</p>

        <img alt="Edge - Network Policy" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshmodel/relationships/edge_firewall_relationship_pod_to_pod.svg" />
        </details>
    </details>

<h2 id="the-meaning-of-relationships">The Meaning of Relationships</h2>

<p>Meshery supports a variety of relationships between components. These relationships are categorized into two types: Semantic and Non-Semantic. Relationships are categorized by whether they are meaningful in terms of how Meshery manages entities - a Semantic relationship - or are simply annotations to aid in the comprehension for you as the designer of the relationship - a Non-Semantic relationship.</p>

<h3 id="semantic-relationships">Semantic Relationships</h3>

<p>Semantic relationships are those that are meaningful in the context of the application or infrastructure. For example, a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Service</code> in Kubernetes is semantically related to a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deployment</code> or a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Pod</code>. These relationships are meaningful and are managed by Meshery.</p>

<h3 id="non-semantic-relationships">Non-Semantic Relationships</h3>

<p>Non-semantic relationships are those that are meaningful to you as a user and your mental representation of your infrastructure and applications, but are not meaningful in terms of how Meshery evaluates the design or manages these relationships and their associated components. Non-semantic relationships are ignored by Meshery’s lifecycle management engine. For example, a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rectangle</code> shape that encloses other components (has a parent relationship with other child components) is not semantically meaningful to the way in which Meshery manages these resources. While the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rectangle</code> shape might have a parent-child relationship with any number of Meshery-managed components, such a relationship does not implicate any management that Meshery might perform; they are not managed by Meshery.</p>

<!-- @iArchitSharma, help, if you would please.

_[TODO: a visual example is needed here]_ -->

<h4 id="identifying-non-semantic-relationships">Identifying Non-Semantic Relationships</h4>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isAnnotation</code> attribute of a Relationship or Component determines whether the given Relationship or Component represents a management concern for Meshery; whether the given Relationship or Component is semantically meaningful, and whose lifecycle is managed by Meshery.</p>

<h2 id="core-concepts-of-relationships">Core Concepts of Relationships</h2>

<ul>
  <li>Kinds</li>
  <li>Types</li>
  <li>Subtypes</li>
  <li>Selectors</li>
  <li>Selectors Sets</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="kind-type-and-subtype-of-relationships">Kind, Type, and Subtype of Relationships</h2>

<p>The combination of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kind</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">type</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">subType</code> uniquely determines the visual paradigm for a given relationship; i.e., relationships with the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">kind</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">type</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">subType</code> will share an identical visual representation regardless of the specific components involved in the relationship.</p>

<h3 id="1-edge---network">1. Edge - Network</h3>

<p>This Relationship type configures the networking between one or more components.</p>

<p><strong>Examples</strong>: An edge-network relationship between a Service and a Deployment or an edge-binding relationship between an Ingress and a Service.</p>

<ul>
  <li>Example 1) Service –&gt; Deployment</li>
  <li>Example 2) IngressController –&gt; Ingress –&gt; Service</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="5-edge---reference">5. Edge - Reference</h3>

<p>Logical or declarative links between components where one component refers to another by name, identifier, type, or scope.</p>

<ul>
  <li>Example 1) Pod –&gt; ConfigMap (via envFrom)</li>
  <li>Example 2) Pod –&gt; Secret (via volumes)</li>
</ul>

<details close=""><summary>Visual Representation of Edge-Reference Relationship</summary>
        <br />
        <p>The <strong>Edge-Reference</strong> relationship type represents a <strong>logical or declarative link</strong> between two components, where one component <strong>refers to another by name, identifier, type, or scope</strong>. This relationship allows components to dynamically locate, associate with, or depend on other components without being tightly coupled to them. It forms the basis for indirect communication, configuration reuse, ownership tracking, and dependency resolution in distributed systems.</p>
        <p>This type of relationship does <strong>not directly provide communication, access, or permission</strong>, but <strong>enables such interactions by declaring intent or pointing to another component</strong>.</p>

<h2 id="selectors-in-relationships">Selectors in Relationships</h2>

<p>In Meshery, a selector is a way to specify which set of components a certain other component should affect or interact with. Selectors provide a flexible and powerful way to manage and orchestrate resources under Meshery’s management.</p>

<p>Selectors can be applied to various components, enabling a wide range of relationship definitions. Here are some examples:</p>

<table class="table table-dark table-active">
    <tr>
        <th>Model Component</th>
        <th>Relationship Kind</th>
        <th>Relationship SubType</th>
        <th>Model Component</th>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Kubernetes ConfigMap</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Kubernetes Pod</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Kubernetes ConfigMap</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Kubernetes Deployment</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td>Meshery WASMFilter</td>
        <td>Hierarchical</td>
        <td>Inventory</td>
        <td>Istio EnvoyFilter</td>
    </tr>
</table>

<p>The above relationships pairs have hierarchical inventory relationships, and visual paradigm remain consistent across different components. A snippet of the selector backing this relationship is listed below.</p>
<details>
<summary>Example Relationship Selector</summary>
<code><pre>
"selector": {
    "allow": {
        "from": [
          {
            "kind": "ConfigMap",
            "model": "kubernetes",
            "patch": {
              "patchStrategy": "replace",
              "mutatorRef": [
                [
                  "name"
                ]
              ],
              "description": "In Kubernetes, ConfigMaps are a versatile resource that can be referenced by various other resources to provide configuration data to applications or other Kubernetes resources.\n\nBy referencing ConfigMaps in these various contexts, you can centralize and manage configuration data more efficiently, allowing for easier updates, versioning, and maintenance of configurations in a Kubernetes environment."
            }
          }
        ],
        "to": [
          {
            "kind": "Pod",
            "model": "kubernetes",
            "patch": {
              "patchStrategy": "replace",
              "mutatedRef": [
                [
                  "settings",
                  "spec",
                  "containers",
                  "_",
                  "envFrom",
                  "0",
                  "configMapRef",
                  "name"
                ]
              ],
              "description": "ConfigMaps can be referenced in the Pod specification to inject configuration data into the Pod's environment.\n\nThe keys from the ConfigMap will be exposed as environment variables to the container within the Pod."
            }
          }
        ]
    }
}
</pre></code>

</details>

<p>The above snippet defines a selector configuration for allowing relationships between <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Kubernetes ConfigMap</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Kubernetes Pod</code>.</p>

<p><!-- add images --></p>

<h2 id="relationship-evaluation">Relationship Evaluation</h2>

<p>Meshery employs a policy-driven approach to evaluate relationships between components. This evaluation helps in:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Determining compatible components for establishing relationships</li>
  <li>Suggesting potential relationships based on the current design</li>
  <li>Validating existing relationships and identifying potential conflicts</li>
  <li>Automating the configuration of components based on established relationships</li>
</ul>

<p>Each invocation of the evaluation process attempts to recursively evaluate the design until it reaches a stable state—i.e., no further changes are detected. If a bug in the evaluation policies causes non-terminating behavior (such as endlessly generating new components), the evaluation will be forcibly stopped after a configurable maximum depth (e.g., 5 iterations), and an error will be raised.</p>

<p>During evaluation, in addition to the input design, the evaluation engine has access to all relationships stored in the registry. These relationships serve as the source of truth for policies to validate existing relationships or identify new ones. Since relationships can be associated with different models, not all of them are relevant to a given design. To ensure efficiency, the evaluation process intelligently filters the registered relationships, retaining only those that directly impact the design.</p>

<p>Currently, the filtering logic includes only relationships from models that are already part of the design. For example, if the design consists solely of Kubernetes components, relationships from the AWS model will not be loaded for evaluation.</p>

<p>Beyond this automatic filtering, relationship evaluation can also be selectively disabled within the design. This is achieved by setting preferences to false for specific relationship categories, defined by their kind, type, and subtype.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/concepts/logical/relationship-evaluation-flow.svg" alt="Meshery Relationship" /></p>

<h3 id="how-relationships-are-formed">How Relationships are formed?</h3>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>You can create relationships manually by using the edge handles, bringing related components to close proximity or dragging a component inside other component. It may happen that, you created a relationship from the UI, but the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/policies">Policy Engine</a> rejected or overrode the decision if all the constraints for a particular relationship are not satisfied.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Relationships are automatically created when a component’s configuration is modified in a way that relationship criteria is satisfied.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Explore an example relationship</h4>
To explore an example of this behavior, see the <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog/deployment/example-edge-permission-relationship-7dd39d30-7b14-4f9f-a66c-06ba3e5000fa.html">Example Edge-Permission Relationship</a> and follow the steps written in its description.
</div>

<p>When the relationships are created by the user, almost in all cases the config of the involved components are patched. To see the specifics of patching refer <a href="#patch-strategies">Patch Strategies</a>.</p>

<p>Designs are evaluated by the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/policies">Policy Engine</a> for potential relationships.</p>

<h3 id="patch-strategies">Patch Strategies</h3>

<p>Patches in Meshery relationships utilize strategies and references (mutatorRef/mutatedRef) for the from and to fields. These convey the property path that will be updated as the relationship is created.</p>

<h3 id="caveats-and-considerations">Caveats and Considerations</h3>

<ol>
  <li>If the user creates a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Hierarchical Inventory</code> relationship between <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Pod</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Job</code>, and any other high-level Kubernetes resources like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deployment</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">StatefulSet</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CronJobs</code>, after the relationship has been established unfortunately, there’s no system to remove the extra pod configuration automatically.
If the design is not configured with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">labels</code> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">selectors</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">replicas</code> appropriately, there’s a possibility of additional resources getting provisioned when deployed. e.g., The relationship between a Pod and deployment can result in 2 Pods (1 pod coming as part of deployment resource) and 1 Deployment.  It’s important to be aware of this possibility and manage configurations carefully to avoid unexpected issues during deployment</li>
</ol>

<h1 id="itemizing-your-relationship-definitions-in-your-meshery-deployment">Itemizing your Relationship Definitions in your Meshery deployment</h1>

<p>In any given Meshery deployment, you can reference and search the full set of registered relationships (in Meshery’s internal registry) using either of Meshery’s client interfaces.</p>

<p><strong>Meshery UI</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>Visit <em>Settings</em> –&gt; <em>Registry</em></li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>Run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">mesheryctl relationship list</code></li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Workspaces</h1>
           <p>Like a Google Drive, Meshery Workspaces serve as a virtual space for your team-based work. Create a Workspace to organize your work and to serve as the central point of collaboration for you and your teams and a central point of access control to Environments and their resources.</p>

<p>You may create Workspaces to organize project-based work or to create domains of responsibility for your teams or segregate Designs and Environments and track team activity.</p>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Your team collaboration point</h4>
Workspaces facilitate collaboration between you and your teams, allow you to control access to resources, and track activity and report on related events.
</div>

<h2 id="key-features">Key Features</h2>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Resource Sharing</strong> Workspaces allow for seamless resource sharing among team members, fostering collaboration.</li>
  <li><strong>Logical Grouping</strong> Within Workspaces, you can group related components such as environments and infrastructure designs.</li>
  <li><strong>Flexibility</strong>: Workspaces support various resources like Kubernetes, Prometheus, Jaeger, Nginx, and more.</li>
  <li><strong>Simplified Management</strong> Managing and deploying resources is made easy within Workspaces.</li>
  <li><strong>Access Control</strong> Workspaces allow you to control access to resources by granting permissions to users and teams.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="workspace-relationships-and-restrictions">Workspace Relationships and Restrictions</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Access to Workspaces may be granted to one or more teams.</li>
  <li>As a point of collaboration to facilitate work, Workspaces may have zero or more Environments associated.</li>
</ul>

<p>After creating a workspace, one of the next steps is to add resources to it. Similar to a shared drive or collection of files, Workspaces function like your Google Drive, while Meshery Designs are comparable to Google Docs.</p>

<h2 id="key-components">Key Components</h2>

<h3 id="environments">Environments</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Environments are a central part of a workspace. They serve as a logical grouping for managing connections. A connection, in this context, can be either managed or discovered by Meshery. Examples of connections include Kubernetes clusters, Prometheus instances, Jaeger traces, Nginx servers, and more.</li>
  <li>One or more environments can be assigned to a workspace.</li>
  <li>Same environment can be assigned to multiple workspaces.</li>
</ul>

<p>See “<a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/environments">Environments</a>” section for more information.</p>

<h3 id="designs">Designs</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Infrastructure Designs are essential for creating reusable deployment templates. Users belonging to teams with access to a workspace can utilize these designs to deploy resources in the Kubernetes clusters associated with that workspace.</li>
  <li>Similar to a shared drive or collection of files, Workspaces function like your Google Drive, while Meshery Designs are comparable to Google Docs.</li>
  <li>One or more designs can be assigned to a workspace.</li>
  <li>Same design can be assigned to multiple workspaces.</li>
</ul>

<p>See “<a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Meshery Designs</a>” section for more information.</p>

<h3 id="organizations">Organizations</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Organizations are the unit of tenancy in Meshery. Organizations group users together.</li>
  <li>Organizations own all resources created by users, like Workspaces, Designs, Environments, and so on.</li>
  <li>Remote Providers can extend Meshery to include additional identity and user management features like hierarchical organizations, or teams (as user groups), and so on.</li>
  <li>Remote Providers can extend Meshery to offer fine-grained permissions and access control to resources like Workspaces, Designs, Environments, and so on.</li>
</ul>

<p>Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/authorization">extensible authorization</a>.
 <!-- "[Organizations](/extensions/team-management)" section for more information. --></p>

<!-- ### Teams

- A Workspace is closely associated with Teams in Meshery. Teams are groups of users with varying permissions, and they are at the center of resource access and management within a Workspace.
- One or more teams can be assigned to a workspace.
- Same team can be assigned to multiple workspaces.

See "[Teams](/extensions/team-management)" section for more information. -->

<h3 id="connections">Connections</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Connections in Meshery refer to various resources that can be either managed or unmanaged, but are discovered and made accessible for use. Examples of Connections include Kubernetes clusters, Prometheus instances, Jaeger services, Nginx deployments, and more. These Connections serve as a fundamental part of Workspaces, as users can deploy infrastructure designs within the context of these Connections.</li>
  <li>Connections can be assigned to one or more environments.</li>
  <li>Same connection can be assigned to multiple environments.</li>
</ul>

<p>See “<a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connections</a>” section for more information.</p>

<h2 id="best-practices">Best Practices</h2>

<p>To make the most of Meshery Workspaces, here are some best practices:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Clearly define permissions in the form of team assignment to ensure proper access control.</li>
  <li>Use Infrastructure Designs to standardize resource deployments.</li>
  <li>Regularly review and update your Workspace’s resources and configurations.</li>
</ul>

<p>Meshery Workspaces enhance collaboration within your teams, providing a structured environment for sharing and managing resources. By following best practices and understanding the core components of Workspaces, you can maximize the benefits of this feature in Meshery.</p>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> App Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-app-mesh">beta</a></td>
    <td>v0.6.4</td>
    <td>v1.4.1</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for App Mesh can install <strong>v1.4.1</strong> of App Mesh. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for App Mesh.</p>

<h3 id="features">Features</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Lifecycle management of App Mesh</li>
  <li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
  <li>Performance testing</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for App Mesh includes a handful of sample applications. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications.</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#emojivoto">Emojivoto</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>A microservice application that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#httpbin">Httpbin</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>Identify overhead involved in running App Mesh, various App Mesh configurations while running different workloads and on different infrastructure. The adapter facilitates data plane and control plane performance testing.</p>

<ol>
  <li>Prometheus integration</li>
  <li>Grafana integration</li>
</ol>

<p>The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-app-mesh">Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</a> will connect to App Mesh’s Prometheus and Grafana instances running in the control plane.</p>
   <br/>

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Cilium</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-cilium">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.2</td>
    <td>v1.10.6</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh can install <strong>v1.10.6</strong> of Cilium. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh.</p>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh is currently under construction (stable state), which means that the adapter is not functional and cannot be interacted with through the <a href="/installation#6-you-will-now-be-directed-to-the-meshery-ui"> Meshery UI </a>at the moment. Check back here to see updates.</p>

<p>Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-cilium">progress</a>.</p>

<h3 id="install-cilium">Install Cilium</h3>

<h5 id="choose-the-meshery-adapter-for-cilium">Choose the Meshery Adapter for Cilium</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<h5 id="click-on--and-choose-the-v1106-of-the-cilium">Click on (+) and choose the v1.10.6 of the Cilium.</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-install.png" />
</a></p>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Consul</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/consul.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/consul-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/consul.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Consul</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-consul">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.3</td>
    <td>v1.8.4</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Consul can install <strong>v1.8.4</strong> of the Consul.</p>

<h3 id="install-consul">Install Consul</h3>

<h5 id="choose-the-meshery-adapter-for-consul">Choose the Meshery Adapter for Consul</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<h5 id="click-on--and-choose-the-v184-of-the-consul">Click on (+) and choose the v1.8.4 of the Consul.</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/consul/consul-install.png" />
</a></p>

<p>A number of <a href="#sample-applications">sample applications</a> for Consul can also be installed using Meshery.</p>

<h3 id="features">Features</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Lifecycle management of Consul</li>
  <li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
  <li>Performance management of Consul and it workloads
    <ul>
      <li>Prometheus and Grafana integration</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Configuration management and best practices of Consul</li>
  <li>Custom configuration</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h3>

<p>Meshery supports the deployment of a variety of sample applications on Meshery Adapter for Consul. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications.</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#httpbin">httpbin</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a>
    <ul>
      <li>The sample BookInfo application displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#imagehub">Image Hub</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Image Hub is a sample application written to run on Consul for exploring WebAssembly modules used as Envoy filters.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="performance-management-of-consul-and-it-workloads">Performance management of Consul and it workloads</h3>

<h4 id="prometheus-and-grafana-integration">Prometheus and Grafana integration</h4>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Consul will connect to Meshery Adapter for Consul’s Prometheus and Grafana instances running in the control plane (typically found in a separate namespace) or other instances to which Meshery has network reachability.</p>

<h3 id="architecture">Architecture</h3>

<p><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/consul/service-mesh-architecture-consul.png"><img src="/extensibility/adapters/consul/service-mesh-architecture-consul.png" alt="Consul Service Mesh Architecture" /></a></p>

<h3 id="suggested-topics">Suggested Topics</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Examine <a href="/architecture">Meshery’s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
  <li>Learn more about <a href="/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>

              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: Meshery Adapters</h1>
           <h2 id="guiding-principles-of-adapter-design">Guiding Principles of Adapter Design</h2>

<p>Adapters allow Meshery to interface with the different cloud native infrastructure. Review the list of all available <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>. See the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture">Meshery Architecture</a> diagrams for visuals on how adapters relate to other Meshery components.
Meshery upholds the following guiding principles for adapter design:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Adapters allow Meshery to interface with the different cloud native infrastructure, exposing their differentiated value to users.</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>Cloud native infrastructure projects should be encouraged to maintain their own adapters. Allowing them to expose their differentiated capabilities encourages this.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>Adapters should avoid wheel reinvention, but seek to leverage the functionality provided by cloud native infrastructure under management.</strong>
    <ul>
      <li>This both reduces sustaining costs and improves reliability.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h2 id="adapters">Adapters</h2>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: center">Adapter</th>
      <th style="text-align: center">Earliest Version</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: center"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/app-mesh.svg" style="width:20px" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/app-mesh">Meshery Adapter for App Mesh</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">                                         v1.4.1</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: center"><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/cilium.svg" style="width:20px" /> <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters/cilium">Meshery Adapter for Cilium Service Mesh</a></td>
      <td style="text-align: center">                                         v1.10.6</td>

<h3 id="adapter-capabilities">Adapter Capabilities</h3>

<p>Meshery communicates with adapters over gRPC. Adapters establish communication with the cloud native infrastructure. Adapters have a predefined set of operations which are grouped based on predefined operation types.</p>

<p>The predefined operation types are:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Install</li>
  <li>Sample application</li>
  <li>Config</li>
  <li>Validate</li>
  <li>Custom</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="meshery-adapter-codebase-overview">Meshery Adapter Codebase Overview</h2>

<p><a href="https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1uQU7e_evJ8IMIzlLoBi3jQSRvpKsl_-K1COVGjJVs30/edit#">Common libraries</a> are used to avoid code duplication and apply DRY.</p>

<h3 id="meshkit"><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit">MeshKit</a></h3>

<p>The code hierarchy is pluggable and independent from one another. There can be N number of packages depending upon the use case.</p>
<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">errors/</code> - holds the implementations and the error handlers and error codes which are used across projects.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">logger/</code> - holds the implementations of logging handler and custom attributes to add if any.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">utils/</code> - holds all the utility functions that are specific to meshery projects and are to be used generically across all of them.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">tracing/</code> - holds the implementations of tracing handlers with different tracing providers like jaeger,newrelic, etc.</li>
</ul>

<p>Each package inside a meshkit is a handler interface implementation, the implementation could be from any third-party packages.</p>

<h3 id="meshery-adapter-library"><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-adapter-library">Meshery Adapter Library</a></h3>

<p>This section contains a high level overview of the meshery-adapter-library, its purpose and architecture. For details, the reader is referred to the documentation and the code in the repository.</p>

<p>The main purpose of the meshery-adapter-library is to:</p>
<ul>
  <li>provide a set of interfaces, some with default implementations, to be used and extended by adapters.</li>
  <li>implement common cross cutting concerns like logging, errors, and tracing</li>
  <li>provide a mini framework implementing the gRPC server that allows plugging in the mesh specific configuration and - operations implemented in the adapters.</li>
  <li>provide middleware extension points</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/meshery-adapter-library.svg"><img src="/assets/img/adapters/meshery-adapter-library.svg" alt="Meshery Adapter Library" /></a></p>

<p><em>Figure: Displaying Meshery Adapter library architecture along with an example of integration</em></p>

<h4 id="overview-and-usage">Overview and Usage</h4>

<p>The library consists of interfaces and default implementations for the main and common functionality of an adapter. It also provides a mini-framework that runs the gRPC adapter service, calling the functions of handlers injected by the adapter code. This is represented in an UML-ish style in the figure pictured. The library is used in all of Meshery’s adapters.</p>

$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

      }

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Istio</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/istio.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/istio-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/istio.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Istio</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-istio">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.3</td>
    <td>v1.6.0</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="features">Features</h2>

<ol>
  <li>Istio Lifecycle Management</li>
  <li>Workload Lifecycle Management</li>
  <li>Cloud Native Performance (SMP)
    <ol>
      <li>Prometheus and Grafana connections</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li>Configuration Analysis, Patterns, and Best Practices
    <ol>
      <li>Custom Configuration</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Istio can install <strong>v1.6.0</strong> of the Istio.</p>

<h3 id="install-istio">Install Istio</h3>

<p>In Meshery’s UI, choose the Meshery Adapter for Istio.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/istio/istio-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/istio/istio-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Click on (+) and choose the v1.6.0 of the Istio.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/istio/istio-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/istio/istio-install.png" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="workload-management">Workload Management</h3>

<p>The (Meshery Adapter for Istio) includes a handful of sample applications. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications:</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a></li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#httpbin">Httpbin</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#online-boutique">Online Boutique</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Online Boutique Application is a web-based, e-commerce demo application from the Google Cloud Platform.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#imagehub">Image Hub</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Image Hub is a sample application written to run on Consul for exploring WebAssembly modules used as Envoy filters.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="using-cloud-native-standards">Using Cloud Native Standards</h2>

<p>Meshery’s powerful performance management functionality is accomplished through implementation of <a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a>. Meshery enables operators to deploy WebAssembly filters to Envoy-based data planes. Meshery facilitates learning about functionality and performance of infrastructure and workloads and incorporates the collection and display of metrics from applications using Prometheus and Grafana integrations.</p>

<h3 id="design-patterns-and-meshery-models">Design Patterns and Meshery Models</h3>

<h3 id="prometheus-and-grafana-connections">Prometheus and Grafana connections</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Istio allows you to quickly deploy (or remove) an Istio add-ons. Meshery will deploy the Prometheus and Grafana add-ons (including Jaeger and Kiali) into Istio’s control plane (typically the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">istio-system</code> namespace). You can also connect Meshery to Prometheus, Grafana instances not running in the control plane.</p>

<p>If you already have existing Prometheus or Grafana deployments in your cluster, MeshSync will discover them and attempt to automatically register them for use.</p>

<h2 id="configuration-management">Configuration Management</h2>

<p>Meshery Adapter for Istio provides</p>

<h3 id="configuration-best-practices">Configuration best practices</h3>

<p>On demand, the Meshery Adapter for Istio will parse all of Istio’s configuration and compare the running configuration of the infrastructure against known best practices for an Meshery Adapter for Istio deployment.</p>

<h3 id="custom-infrastructure-configuration">Custom infrastructure configuration</h3>

<p>Meshery allows you to apply configuration to your infrastructure deployment. You can paste (or type in) any Kubernetes manifest that you would like to have applied to your infrastructure, in fact, you can apply any configuration that you would like to your Kubernetes cluster. This configuration may be VirtualServices, DestinationRules or any other custom Istio resource.</p>

<p><a href="istio-adapter-custom-configuration.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/istio/istio-adapter-custom-configuration.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Add-on resources can be applied <strong>or</strong> deleted using this custom configuration operation.</p>

<h3 id="suggested-topics">Suggested Topics</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Examine <a href="/architecture">Meshery’s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
  <li>Learn more about <a href="/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Kuma</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/kuma.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Kuma</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-kuma">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.1</td>
    <td>v1.2.2</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Kuma can install <strong>v1.2.2</strong> of Kuma infrastructure. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Kuma.</p>

<h3 id="install-kuma">Install Kuma</h3>

<p>Choose the Meshery Adapter for Kuma.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/kuma/kuma-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/kuma/kuma-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Click on (+) and choose the v1.2.2 of the Kuma infrastructure.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/kuma/kuma-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/kuma/kuma-install.png" />
</a></p>

<h2 id="workload-management">Workload Management</h2>

<p>The following sample applications are available in this adapter.</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps#bookinfo">Bookinfo</a>
    <ul>
      <li>The sample BookInfo application displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
