        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Linkerd</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/linkerd.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Linkerd</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-linkerd">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.2</td>
    <td>v2.10.2</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h3 id="features">Features</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Lifecycle management of Linkerd</li>
  <li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
  <li>Performance testing</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Linkerd can install <strong>v2.10.2</strong> of Linkerd. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Linkerd.</p>

<h3 id="install-linkerd">Install Linkerd</h3>

<p>Note: Linkerd’s control plane will be deployed to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">linkerd</code> namespace. Linkerd does not support deployments of its control plane into namespaces under a different name.</p>

<h5 id="choose-the-meshery-adapter-for-linkerd">Choose the Meshery Adapter for Linkerd</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<h5 id="click-on--and-choose-the-v2102-of-the-linkerd">Click on (+) and choose the v2.10.2 of the Linkerd.</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/linkerd/linkerd-install.png" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Linkerd includes the ability to deploy a variety of sample applications. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Emojivoto</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>A microservice application that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Bookinfo</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>The sample BookInfo application displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Linkerd Books</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>A sample application built for demonstrating manage your bookshelf.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">HTTPbin</a></p>
    <ul>
      <li>A simple HTTP Request &amp; Response Service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>Identify overhead involved in running Linkerd, various Linkerd configurations while running different workloads and on different infrastructure. The adapter facilitates data plane and control plane performance testing.</p>

<ol>
  <li>Prometheus integration</li>
  <li>Grafana integration</li>
</ol>

<p>The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-linkerd">Meshery Adapter for Linkerd</a> will connect to Linkerd’s Prometheus and Grafana instances running in the control plane.</p>
   <br/>


        </div>
      </main>

              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class

              $(this).addClass('selected');

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm-white.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/nginx-sm.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> NGINX Service Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-nginx-sm">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.8.1</td>
    <td>v1.2.0</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh is currently under construction (stable state). Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-nginx-sm">progress</a>.</p>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh can install <strong>v1.2.0</strong> of NGINX Service Mesh ewE E . A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh.</p>

<h3 id="features">Features</h3>

<ol>
  <li>Lifecycle management of NGINX Service Mesh</li>
  <li>Lifecycle management of sample applications</li>
  <li>Performance testing</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for NGINX Service Mesh includes a handful of sample applications. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications.</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Emojivoto</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>A microservice application that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Bookinfo</a></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Httpbin</a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><a href="https://github.com/BuoyantIO/booksapp">NGINX Books</a></p>
    <ul>
      <li>Application that helps you manage your bookshelf.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>Identify overhead involved in running NGINX Service Mesh, various NGINX Service Mesh configurations while running different workloads and on different infrastructure. The adapter facilitates data plane and control plane performance testing.</p>

<ol>
  <li>Prometheus integration</li>
  <li>Grafana integration</li>
</ol>

   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/nsm.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/nsm.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/nsm.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Network Service Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-nsm">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.5.4</td>
    <td>v0.2.1</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management-of-meshery-adapter-for-network-service-mesh">Lifecycle management of Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh can install <strong>v0.2.1</strong> of Network Service Mesh. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh.</p>

<h3 id="install-network-service-mesh">Install Network Service Mesh</h3>

<h5 id="choose-the-meshery-adapter-for-network-service-mesh">Choose the Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh</h5>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/nsm-adapter.png">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/nsm-adapter.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Click on (+) and choose the v0.2.1 of the Network Service Mesh.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/nsm-install.png">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/nsm-install.png" />
</a></p>

<h2 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h2>

<p>The (Meshery Adapter for Network Service Mesh) includes a handful of sample applications. These applications represent different network services orchestrated by Network Service Mesh. Use Meshery to deploy any of these sample applications:</p>

<h3 id="1-hello-nsm-application">1. Hello NSM Application</h3>

<p>Watch this presentation to see the Hello NSM Application in-action:</p>

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/4xKixsDTtdM" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>

<p>See on YouTube: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4xKixsDTtdM&amp;list=PL3A-A6hPO2IOpTbdH89qR-4AE0ON13Zie">Adopting Network Service Mesh with Meshery</a></p>

<h4 id="2-vpp-icmp-application">2. VPP-ICMP Application</h4>

<p><em>A simple example that connects a vpp based Pod to a Network Service using memif.</em></p>

<p>The simplest possible case for Network Service Mesh is to have is connecting a Client via a vWire to another Pod that is providing a Network Service.
Network Service Mesh allows flexibility in the choice of mechanisms used to provide that vWire to a workload.</p>

<p>The icmp responder example does this with kernel interfaces. The vpp-icmp-responder provides and consumes the same ‘icmp-responder’ Network Service, but has Client’s and Endpoint’s that use a <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aVr32WgY0Q">memif</a> high speed memory interfaces to achieve performance unavailable via kernel interfaces.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example.svg">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example.svg" />
</a></p>

<p>Working process</p>

<p>This will install two Deployments:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Name</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">vpp-icmp-responder-nsc</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">The Clients (four replicas)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">vpp-icmp-responder-nse</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">The Endpoints (two replicas)</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>And cause each Client to get a vWire connecting it to one of the Endpoints. Network Service Mesh handles the Network Service Discovery and Routing, as well as the vWire ‘Connection Handling’ for setting all of this up.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example-2.svg">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example-2.svg" />
</a></p>

<p>In order to make this case more interesting, Endpoint1 and Endpoint2 are deployed on two separate Nodes using PodAntiAffinity, so that the Network Service Mesh has to demonstrate the ability to string vWires between Clients and Endpoints on the same Node and Clients and Endpoints on different Nodes.</p>

<p>Verification</p>

<p>First verify that the vpp-icmp-responder example Pods are all up and running:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 $ kubectl get pods | grep vpp-icmp-responder
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<p>To see the vpp-icmp-responder example in action, you can run:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 $ curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/networkservicemesh/networkservicemesh/master/scripts/nsc_ping_all.sh | bash
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<h4 id="3-icmp-responder">3. ICMP Responder</h4>

<p>The simplest possible case for Network Service Mesh is to have is connecting a Client via a vWire to another Pod that is providing a Network Service. We call this case the ‘icmp-responder’ example, because it allows the client to ping the IP address of the Endpoint over the vWire.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example.svg">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/vpp-icmp-responder-example.svg" />
</a></p>

<p>Outcomes</p>

<p>This will install two Deployments:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style="text-align: left">Name</th>
      <th style="text-align: left">Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">icmp-responder-nsc</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">The Clients, four replicas</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="text-align: left">icmp-responder-nse</td>
      <td style="text-align: left">The Endpoints, two replicas</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>And cause each Client to get a vWire connecting it to one of the Endpoints. Network Service Mesh handles the
Network Service Discovery and Routing, as well as the vWire ‘Connection Handling’ for setting all of this up.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/icmp-responder-example-2.svg">
  <img style="width:500px; background: white" src="/v0.8/assets/img/adapters/nsm/icmp-responder-example-2.svg" />
</a></p>

<p>In order to make this case more interesting, Endpoint1 and Endpoint2 are deployed on two separate Nodes using
<em>PodAntiAffinity</em>, so that the Network Service Mesh has to demonstrate the ability to string vWires between Clients and
Endpoints on the same Node and Clients and Endpoints on different Nodes.</p>

<p>Verification</p>

<ol>
  <li>Verify that the icmp-responder example Pods are all up and running:</li>
</ol>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 $ kubectl get pods | grep icmp-responder
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<ol>
  <li>To see the icmp-responder example in action, you may run:</li>
</ol>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">
 $ curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/networkservicemesh/networkservicemesh/master/scripts/nsc_ping_all.sh | bash
 </div></div>
 </pre>

<h3 id="suggested-topics">Suggested Topics</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Examine <a href="/architecture">Meshery’s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
  <li>Learn more about <a href="/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>

        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)

              $(document).find(toc).append(content);

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link

        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Tanzu Service Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/tanzu.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/tanzu.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/tanzu.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Tanzu Service Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-tanzu-sm">alpha</a></td>
    <td>v0.1.0</td>
    <td>pre-GA</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Tanzu Service Mesh can install <strong>pre-GA</strong> of Tanzu Service Mesh. A number of sample applications for Tanzu Service Mesh can also be installed using Meshery.</p>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Tanzu Service Mesh is currently under construction (alpha state), which means that the adapter is not functional and cannot be interacted with through the <a href="/installation#6-you-will-now-be-directed-to-the-meshery-ui"> Meshery UI </a>at the moment. Check back here to see updates.</p>

<p>Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-tanzu-sm">progress</a>.</p>

<h3 id="suggested-reading">Suggested Reading</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Examine <a href="/architecture">Meshery’s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
  <li>Learn more about <a href="/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Meshery Adapter for Traefik Mesh</h1>
           
<table style="display: flex; align-self: center; justify-self: center">
  <th>Cloud Native Infrastructure</th>
  <th>Adapter Status</th>
  <th>Adapter Version</th>
  <th>Earliest Supported Infrastructure Version</th>
  <tr>
    <td><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/service-meshes/traefik-mesh.svg" style="width:20px" data-logo-for-dark="/assets/img/service-meshes/traefik-mesh.svg" data-logo-for-light="/assets/img/service-meshes/traefik-mesh.svg" id="logo-dark-light" loading="lazy" /> Traefik Mesh</td>
    <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-traefik-mesh">stable</a></td>
    <td>v0.6.9</td>
    <td>v1.0</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="lifecycle-management">Lifecycle management</h2>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Traefik Mesh can install <strong>v1.0</strong> of Traefik Mesh. A number of sample applications can be installed using the Meshery Adapter for Traefik Mesh.</p>

<p>Want to contribute? Check our <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery-traefik-mesh">progress</a>.</p>

<h3 id="sample-applications">Sample Applications</h3>

<p>The Meshery Adapter for Traefik Mesh includes some sample applications operations. Meshery can be used to deploy any of these sample applications.</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Bookinfo</a></li>
  <li><a href="/v0.8/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps">Httpbin</a>
    <ul>
      <li>Httpbin is a simple HTTP request and response service.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suggested-topics">Suggested Topics</h2>

<ul>
  <li>Examine <a href="/architecture">Meshery’s architecture</a> and how adapters fit in as a component.</li>
  <li>Learn more about <a href="/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>.</li>
</ul>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: APIs</h1>
           <h2 id="mesherys-apis">Meshery’s APIs</h2>

<p>Each of Meshery’s APIs are subject to the following authentication and authorization system. The REST and GraphQL APIs are available on the same network port you use to connect to Meshery UI, which is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">9081/tcp</code> by default. Each of the API endpoints are exposed through <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/router/server.go">server.go</a>. Endpoints are grouped by function (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/system/version</code>). Additionally, <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Remote Providers</a> can extend Meshery’s endpoints behind the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/extensions/</code> endpoint.</p>

<h3 id="api-reference">API Reference</h3>

<div class="tab-container">
  <!-- Tab 1: REST API -->
  <input id="tab1" type="radio" name="tabs" checked="" />
  <label for="tab1" data-icon="&#xf1cb;">REST API</label>
  <section class="tabbed" id="content1">
    <p>Meshery Server's REST API is available at <code>[hostname]:[port]/api/</code>.</p>
    <div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Meshery's REST API Reference</h4>
See <a href="/v0.8/reference/rest-apis">REST API Reference</a> Self-generated API documentation for Meshery's REST API. Documentation is generated from Meshery's Open API schema.
</div>

  </section>

  <!-- Tab 2: GraphQL API -->
  <input id="tab2" type="radio" name="tabs" />
  <label for="tab2" data-icon="&#xf17d;">GraphQL API</label>
  <section class="tabbed" id="content2">
    <p>Meshery Server's GraphQl API is available at <code>{hostname]:[port]/api/graphql/query</code>. A GraphQL request can be made as a POST request to the endpoint with the query as the payload. Meshery Server's GraphQL API can be used to perform three operations:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Queries for data retrieval.</li>
      <li>Mutations for creating, updating, and deleting data.</li>
      <li>Subscriptions for watching for any data changes.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>Explore the Meshery GraphQL API using the interactive Playground provided with Meshery instance at http://localhost:9081/api/system/graphql/playground.</p>
    <div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Meshery's GraphQL API Reference</h4>
See <a href="/v0.8/reference/graphql-apis">GraphQL API Reference</a> Self-generated API documentation for Meshery's GraphQL API. The API can be explored interactively using the GraphQL Playground. Documentation is generated from Meshery's GraphQL schema. Each table below documents a GraphQL type.
</div>

  </section>
</div>

<h3 id="authentication">Authentication</h3>

<p>Requests to any of the API endpoints must be authenticated and include a valid JWT access token in the HTTP headers. Type of authentication is determined by the selected <a href="#providers">Provider</a>. Use of the Local Provider, “None”, puts Meshery into single-user mode and does not require authentication.</p>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">What are authentication tokens?</h4>
Meshery authentication tokens allow users or systems to authenticate with Meshery Server via either its two clients, <a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl">Meshery &gt;CLI</a> and <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/api#how-to-get-your-token">UI</a>, or its two APIs: <a href="/v0.8/reference/rest-apis">REST</a> or <a href="/v0.8/reference/graphql-apis">GraphQL</a>. <p>Meshery's authentication token system provide secure access to Meshery's powerful management features.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="how-to-get-your-token">How to get your token</h3>

<p>There are two ways to get your authentication token:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Meshery UI</li>
  <li>Meshery CLI</li>
</ol>

<p>Using Meshery UI, you can get a copy of your authentication token by following these steps:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Log into Meshery by selecting your identity provider of choice (typically found at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http:&lt;meshery-server&gt;:9081/provider</code>)</li>
  <li>Navigate to your user’s avatar in the upper lefthand corner and select “Get Token” from the dropdown of profile section.</li>
</ol>

<p>Using Meshery CLI, you can get a copy of your authentication token by executing this command:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system login</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>In order to use this command, you must have a web browser available on your system (this command cannot be executed on a headless system).</p>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">How to use the token for requests to Meshery Rest API using API clients</h4>
 Download your token from Meshery UI and copy the token value from the downloaded file, this will be used for authentication.
</div>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">meshery-provider: Meshery
token: your token</code>
</div>
</pre>
<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading"></h4>
Navigate to the cookies section your API testing platform, to set the appropriate name and value for the cookie, then make sure to save the configured cookies to initiate the request. <p> The request will be sent to the Meshery API using the configured cookies for authentication</p>
</div>

<h3 id="endpoints">Endpoints</h3>

<p>Each of the API endpoints are exposed through <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/router/server.go">server.go</a>. Endpoints are grouped by function (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/mesh</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/perf</code>).</p>

<p>Alternatively, <a href="./providers">Remote Providers</a> can extend Meshery’s endpoints behind the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/api/extensions/</code> endpoint.</p>

<h2 id="authorization">Authorization</h2>

<p>While Meshery only requires a valid token in order to allow clients to invoke its APIs, Remote Providers can optionally enforce key-based permissions.</p>
   <br/>


        </div>
      </main>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: Authorization</h1>
           <p>Meshery features an extensible authorization system that offers the ability to deliver fine-grained access control across it’s web-based user interface, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture">Meshery UI</a>.</p>

<h2 id="authorization-keys">Authorization Keys</h2>

<p>The extensible authorization system consists of a large set of keys. Each key uniquely represents a specific capability, for example, the ability to view a <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/connections">Connection</a>, edit or delete a Connection. With the help of these keys, the system evaluates the permissions during runtime and renders UI both helping offer a secure management system and a customizable user experience.</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Note</h4>
The extensible authorization system is available to both Local and Remote Providers. Depending upon your chosen <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">Remote Provider</a>, keys, clustering of them, assigning them to user groups, not just individual users or to user roles may be offered.
</div>

<h2 id="authorization-framework">Authorization Framework</h2>

<p>Meshery utilizes CASL (JS-based permission framework) to evaluate any given user’s set of session keys against the built-in keyhooks populated through each invidual Meshery UI page. This allows for granular control over the UI, empowering you to tailor your Meshery experience to your organization’s needs by limiting access to specific features and functionalities based on the user’s assigned keys.</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/permission-in-UI.png">
  <img style="width:min(100%,800px)" src="/v0.8/assets/img/permission-in-UI.png" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="introduction-to-casljs">Introduction to CASL.js</h3>

<p><a href="https://casl.js.org">CASL.js</a> is an isomorphic authorization JavaScript library which restricts what resources a given client is allowed to access. It’s designed to be incrementally adoptable and can easily scale between a simple claim based and fully featured subject and attribute based authorization. It makes it easy to manage and share permissions/keys across UI components, API services, and database queries.</p>

<p>An example of how CASL evaluate permission in UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;React.Fragment&gt;
	{!CAN(keys.DELETE_CONNECTION.action, keys.DELETE_CONNECTION.subject) &amp;&amp; (
		&lt;Button id=&quot;delete-connection&quot;&gt;Delete&lt;Button/&gt;
	)}
&lt;/React.Fragment&gt; 
</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Once a user has logged in, the backend will send a response with the permissions that the user has. Those permissions will be used to create abilities on the frontend, CASL gets updated with those abilities. The UI maintains a constant file containing all allowed permissions, referred to as keys. With the help of these keys, CAN function evaluates the permissions during runtime and renders UI.</p>

<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Note</h4>

It's important to understand not all pages uses CASL authorization, means even if you are not assigned with any role within organization you might access preferences page and Meshery UI dashboard.
</div>

<h2 id="authorization-using-local-provider">Authorization using Local Provider</h2>

<p>Meshery’s built-in identity provider, “Local” Provider, operates with a large set of predefined keys interspersed throughout Meshery UI and persisted in <a href="/v0.8/concepts/architecture/database">Meshery Database</a>. These keys are used to evaluate the permissions of a given user and render the UI accordingly. The keys are grouped into three categories: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">action</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">subject</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">object</code>.</p>

<div class="alert alert-dark">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Discussion Forum</h4>
Don't find an answer to your question here? Ask on the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">Discussion Forum</a>.
</div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility: Build-time</h1>
           <p>Meshery supports build-time extensibility, allowing system integrators to customize the Meshery container image during the Docker build process. This extension point enables organizations to inject custom configurations, data, provider extensions, and other resources directly into the Meshery container image at build-time.</p>

<h2 id="build-time-extension-point">Build-time Extension Point</h2>

<p>The build-time extension point allows you to supply custom content by placing a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory at the root of the Meshery repository before building the Docker image. The contents of this directory will be copied into the container image and made available to Meshery at runtime.</p>

<h3 id="how-it-works">How It Works</h3>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Placement</strong>: Create a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory at the root of the Meshery repository (same level as the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Dockerfile</code>).</li>
  <li><strong>Content</strong>: Add any build-time configuration, data, packages, or other resources you want to include in the container image to this directory.</li>
  <li><strong>Build</strong>: Run <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docker build</code> as usual. The Docker build process will automatically copy the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory and its contents into the container image at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.meshery/</code>.</li>
  <li><strong>Runtime Access</strong>: The injected content will be available to Meshery at runtime under <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.meshery/</code>.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="directory-structure">Directory Structure</h3>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>meshery/                     # Repository root
├── .meshery/               # Build-time extension directory (optional)
│   ├── config/            # Custom configuration files
│   ├── provider/          # Provider-specific extensions
│   ├── content/           # Custom patterns, filters, applications
│   └── ...                # Any other custom content
├── install/
│   └── docker/
│       └── Dockerfile     # Main Dockerfile
└── ...
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="example-use-cases">Example Use Cases</h3>

<h4 id="custom-configuration-files">Custom Configuration Files</h4>

<p>Place custom configuration files that should be bundled with your Meshery deployment:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> .meshery/config
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"custom_setting=value"</span> <span class="o">&gt;</span> .meshery/config/custom.conf
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="provider-specific-extensions">Provider-specific Extensions</h4>

<p>Include proprietary or organization-specific provider extensions:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> .meshery/provider/MyProvider/v1.0.0
<span class="nb">cp</span> /path/to/provider-extension.tar.gz .meshery/provider/MyProvider/v1.0.0/
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="custom-content">Custom Content</h4>

<p>Add organization-specific patterns, filters, or applications:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> .meshery/content/patterns
<span class="nb">cp</span> /path/to/custom-patterns/<span class="k">*</span> .meshery/content/patterns/
</code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="pre-installed-models">Pre-installed Models</h4>

<p>Include pre-downloaded models or manifests that might not be available at runtime:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> .meshery/models
<span class="nb">cp</span> <span class="nt">-r</span> /path/to/custom-models/<span class="k">*</span> .meshery/models/
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="building-with-build-time-extensions">Building with Build-time Extensions</h3>

<p>To build a Meshery container image with your custom build-time extensions:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Create your .meshery directory with custom content</span>
<span class="nb">mkdir</span> <span class="nt">-p</span> .meshery/config
<span class="nb">echo</span> <span class="s2">"my_config=value"</span> <span class="o">&gt;</span> .meshery/config/custom.conf

<span class="c"># Build the Docker image (from the repository root)</span>
docker build <span class="nt">-f</span> <span class="nb">install</span>/docker/Dockerfile <span class="nt">-t</span> meshery:custom <span class="nb">.</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The build process will:</p>
<ol>
  <li>Copy all files from the build context (including <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory)</li>
  <li>Extract the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory in a build stage</li>
  <li>Copy the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory contents to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.meshery/</code> in the final image</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="runtime-behavior">Runtime Behavior</h3>

<p>At runtime, Meshery will have access to:</p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Seed Content</strong>: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.meshery/seed_content/</code> (standard Meshery seed content)</li>
  <li><strong>Config</strong>: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.meshery/config/</code> (Meshery configuration files)</li>
  <li><strong>Custom Content</strong>: Any additional content you placed in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery/</code> during build</li>
</ul>

<p>Your custom content in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery/</code> will be merged with the standard Meshery directories. The contents are owned by the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">appuser</code> user in the container.</p>

<h3 id="important-notes">Important Notes</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Optional</strong>: The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory is optional. If not present during build, the Docker build will continue without errors.</li>
  <li><strong>Merge Behavior</strong>: If you create subdirectories with the same names as existing Meshery directories (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">config</code>), the contents will be merged.</li>
  <li><strong>Permissions</strong>: All files copied from the build-time <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory will be owned by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">appuser:appuser</code> in the container.</li>
  <li><strong>Not in Version Control</strong>: The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory at the repository root is typically not committed to version control. Add it to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.gitignore</code> if you’re creating temporary build-time extensions.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="security-considerations">Security Considerations</h3>

<p>When using build-time extensions:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Review Content</strong>: Always review the contents of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory before building to ensure no sensitive information or malicious content is included.</li>
  <li><strong>Secrets Management</strong>: Do not include secrets, passwords, or API keys in the build-time <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory. Use environment variables or runtime configuration for sensitive data.</li>
  <li><strong>Trust Sources</strong>: Only include content from trusted sources to avoid introducing security vulnerabilities.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="comparison-with-runtime-extension-points">Comparison with Runtime Extension Points</h3>

<p>Meshery supports multiple <a href="/v0.8/extensibility">extension points</a> at different stages:</p>

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Extension Point</th>
      <th>When</th>
      <th>Use Case</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/build-time">Build-time</a></strong></td>
      <td>During <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">docker build</code></td>
      <td>Pre-package custom configurations, offline packages, proprietary plugins</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/v0.8/extensibility">Boot-time</a></strong></td>
      <td>Container startup</td>
      <td>Dynamic configuration that can change between deployments</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/v0.8/extensibility">Runtime</a></strong></td>
      <td>While Meshery is running</td>
      <td>User-installed plugins, dynamically loaded extensions</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>Choose the build-time extension point when you need to:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Bundle organization-specific customizations in a custom container image</li>
  <li>Include content that must be available before Meshery starts</li>
  <li>Create a self-contained deployment with all dependencies pre-packaged</li>
  <li>Deploy in air-gapped or restricted network environments</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</h3>

<p><strong>My <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory isn’t being copied</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>Ensure the directory is at the repository root (same level as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">install/docker/Dockerfile</code>)</li>
  <li>Check that the directory isn’t excluded in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.dockerignore</code></li>
  <li>Verify the build context includes the repository root</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Permission denied errors at runtime</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>The build process should automatically set ownership to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">appuser:appuser</code></li>
  <li>If issues persist, check file permissions in your source <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Build fails with “no such file or directory”</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>This should not happen as the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.meshery</code> directory is optional</li>
  <li>If you see this error, check your Docker version and build logs</li>
</ul>
   <br/>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Extensibility</h1>
           <p>Meshery has an extensible architecture with several different types of extension points.</p>

<p><!-- via [adapters](/extensibility/adapters), different [load generators](/extensibility/load-generators) and different [providers](/extensibility/providers). Meshery also offers a REST API. --></p>

<h2 id="extension-points">Extension Points</h2>

<p>Meshery is not just an application. It is a set of microservices where the central component is itself called Meshery. Integrators may extend Meshery by taking advantage of designated Extension Points. Extension points come in various forms and are available through Meshery’s architecture.</p>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/architecture/meshery_extension_points.svg" alt="Meshery Extension Points" /></p>

<p><em>Figure: Extension points available throughout Meshery</em></p>

<!-- 
1. [Adapters](/extensibility/adapters)
   -  Messaging Framework (CloudEvents and NATS) 
1. [GraphQL API](/extensibility/api#graphql)
1. [Load Generators](/extensibility/load-generators)
1. [Providers](/extensibility/providers)
1. [REST API](/extensibility/api#rest)
1. [UI Plugins](extensibility/ui)
1. [Integrations](/extensibility/integrations)
1. [Extensions](/extensibility/extensions) 
-->

<h2 id="types-of-extension-points">Types of Extension Points</h2>

<p>The following points of extension are currently incorporated into Meshery.</p>

<ul>
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters">Extensibility: Meshery Adapters</a>
      
              - Meshery architecture is extensible. Meshery provides several extension points for working with different cloud native infrastructure via <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/adapters">adapters</a>, <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/load-generators">load generators</a> and <a href="/v0.8/extensibility/providers">providers</a>.
            
            </li>
            
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/api">Extensibility: APIs</a>
      
              - Meshery architecture is extensible, offering an array of extension points and REST and GraphQL APIs.
            
            </li>
            
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/build-time">Extensibility: Build-time</a>
      
              - System integrators can supply build-time configuration, data, packages, and other extensions to Meshery's container image.
            
            </li>
            
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/authorization">Extensibility: Authorization</a>
      
              - Meshery architecture is extensible. Meshery provides several extension points for working with different cloud native projects via authorization, adapters, load generators and providers.
            
            </li>
            
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    <li><a href="/v0.8/extensibility/load-generators">Extensibility: Load Generators</a>
      
              - Meshery offers support for more types of Kubernetes and cloud native infrastructure than any other project or product in the world. Meshery uses adapters for more deeply managing specific types of infrastructure.
            
            </li>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Azure Operator</h1>
           Collaborative and visual infrastructure as design for Azure Operator



<!-- components -->
<div>
    <section class="Compheading">
        
    </section>

    </section>
</div>
<!-- components end -->





  


<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);

             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);

<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<h2>What are Meshery Models and Components?</h2>

<p>Meshery Models and Components represent the fundamental building blocks of your infrastructure. Use them to define the structure and configuration of your infrastructure and deployments by incorporating their use into a Design. Think of Designs as blueprints or templates that encapsulate everything from network configurations to service definitions.</p>

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/models">Models</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/components">Components</a>, <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/relationships">Relationships</a>, and <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/designs">Designs</a></h6>

<h2>What is the Meshery Registry</h2>

The Meshery Registry is a vital component within Meshery, serving as a centralized repository for managing a diverse range of cloud and cloud native resources. It stores and organizes crucial information such as models, categories, components, and relationships, enabling efficient interaction and utilization of these resources within the Meshery ecosystem. You can conveniently access and manage registry data through Meshery UI, and through Meshery CLI (<a href="/v0.8/reference/mesheryctl/registry">mesheryctl registry</a>).

<h6 class="integration">Learn more about the <a href="/v0.8/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a></h6>
